import Mathlib
/-! QED-E068: Singularities of the permanental hypersurface
The hypersurface where the n×n determinant vanishes has rational singularities. Decide whether the
hypersurface where the n×n permanent vanishes has rational singularities for every n (and compute
its minimal exponent).
Informal statement: Let X_n = {per_n = 0} ⊂ 𝔸^{n²}_ℂ and α̃(X_n) Saito's minimal exponent (the
smallest root of b_{per_n}(−s)/(1−s)). X_n has rational singularities iff α̃(X_n) > 1. Decide whether
X_n has rational singularities for every n (Claim: yes). Known: α̃(X_2) = 2; for det_n,
b(s) = ∏_{i=1}^n (s+i), so α̃ = 2. The sharper questions (exact value of α̃(X_n), e.g. n = 3; is
α̃(X_n) = 2 for all n?) are not part of Claim.
Formalization notes: The Bernstein–Sato polynomial b_f is the monic generator of the ideal of
b ∈ ℂ[s] for which there is an operator P(s) = ∑_{j,α} s^j c_{j,α}(x) ∂^α in D_n[s] with
P(s) f^{s+1} = b(s) f^s. Because the evaluation s ↦ m, f^s ↦ f^m is a D-module map to ℂ[x]_f and a
polynomial identity in s holding at all m ∈ ℕ holds identically, this functional identity is
equivalent to the polynomial identities ∑ m^j c_{j,α} ∂^α(f^{m+1}) = b(m) f^m for all m ∈ ℕ, which
is how `IsBMultiple` is stated (∂^α via iterated `MvPolynomial.pderiv`). Saito: rational
singularities ⇔ α̃ > 1 ⇔ b_f(s) = (s+1)q(s) with every root of q < −1. Since b_f divides every
admissible b and (s+1) | b_f, this is equivalent to: some admissible b has the form (s+1)q with q ≠ 0
and all roots of q having real part < −1 (roots of b-functions are negative rationals). n = 0 is
excluded (per_0 = 1 is a unit).
Proving `Claim` = per_n has rational singularities for all n ≥ 1 (exhibit such operators).
Proving `¬Claim` = for some n, α̃(per_n) ≤ 1 (non-rational singularities).
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE068

/-- The n×n permanent as a polynomial in the n² entries. -/
noncomputable def per (n : ℕ) : MvPolynomial (Fin n × Fin n) ℂ :=
  ∑ π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), ∏ i : Fin n, MvPolynomial.X (i, π i)

/-- Iterated partial derivative `∂^α g` (the partials commute, so the order is irrelevant). -/
noncomputable def iterPDeriv {σ : Type*} [Fintype σ] [DecidableEq σ] (α : σ →₀ ℕ)
    (g : MvPolynomial σ ℂ) : MvPolynomial σ ℂ :=
  (Finset.univ : Finset σ).toList.foldr
    (fun i acc => (⇑(MvPolynomial.pderiv i : Derivation ℂ (MvPolynomial σ ℂ) (MvPolynomial σ ℂ)))^[α i] acc) g

/-- `b` lies in the Bernstein–Sato ideal of `f`: some `P(s) = ∑ s^j c_{j,α} ∂^α` satisfies
`P(s) f^{s+1} = b(s) f^s`, written via the equivalent identities at every `s = m ∈ ℕ`. -/
def IsBMultiple {σ : Type*} [Fintype σ] [DecidableEq σ] (f : MvPolynomial σ ℂ)
    (b : Polynomial ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (S : Finset (ℕ × (σ →₀ ℕ))) (c : ℕ × (σ →₀ ℕ) → MvPolynomial σ ℂ),
    ∀ m : ℕ,
      ∑ jα ∈ S, MvPolynomial.C ((m : ℂ) ^ jα.1) * c jα * iterPDeriv jα.2 (f ^ (m + 1)) =
        MvPolynomial.C (b.eval (m : ℂ)) * f ^ m

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∃ q : Polynomial ℂ, q ≠ 0 ∧ (∀ r : ℂ, q.IsRoot r → r.re < -1) ∧
    IsBMultiple (per n) ((Polynomial.X + 1) * q)

end OpenProblems.QEDE068

title: Charge on a Fermat conductor
plain: Put a unit of electric charge on a perfectly conducting solid x^4+y^4+z^4 <= 1. Show that the surface charge is thinnest exactly at the six flat points (+-1,0,0),... and thickest exactly at the eight points in the diagonal directions.
math: Let $K=\{x^4+y^4+z^4\le1\}\subset\mathbb R^3$ and let $\mu=\rho\,d\sigma$ be its Newtonian (capacitary) equilibrium measure, $\sigma$ surface measure on $\partial K$ ($\rho$ is real-analytic and positive since $\partial K$ is analytic). Prove that $\min_{\partial K}\rho$ is attained exactly at $(\pm1,0,0),(0,\pm1,0),(0,0,\pm1)$ and $\max_{\partial K}\rho$ exactly at $3^{-1/4}(\pm1,\pm1,\pm1)$.

import Mathlib
/-! QED-E069: Charge on a Fermat conductor
Put a unit of electric charge on the perfectly conducting solid x⁴ + y⁴ + z⁴ ≤ 1. The claim is that
the surface charge density is smallest exactly at the six flat points (±1,0,0), (0,±1,0), (0,0,±1)
and largest exactly at the eight diagonal points 3^{-1/4}(±1,±1,±1).
Informal statement: Let K = {x⁴+y⁴+z⁴ ≤ 1} ⊂ ℝ³ and let μ = ρ dσ be its Newtonian (capacitary)
equilibrium measure, σ surface measure on ∂K (ρ is real-analytic and positive since ∂K is analytic).
Prove that min_{∂K} ρ is attained exactly at (±1,0,0),(0,±1,0),(0,0,±1) and max_{∂K} ρ exactly at
3^{-1/4}(±1,±1,±1).
Formalization notes: ℝ³ is `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)` (Euclidean distance), coordinates via
`EuclideanSpace.proj`. The boundary ∂K is written explicitly as S = {x⁴+y⁴+z⁴ = 1}. Surface measure
is the 2-dimensional Hausdorff measure restricted to S; Mathlib's `hausdorffMeasure 2` is not
normalized to area, but it differs from surface area by a constant factor, which only rescales ρ and
does not affect where ρ is extremal. The equilibrium density is characterized as a continuous ρ with
total charge ∫_S ρ dσ = 1 whose single-layer potential ∫_S ρ(y)/|x−y| dσ(y) is constant on K. This
density exists (classical potential theory, ∂K analytic) and is unique on S (a zero-charge single
layer with constant potential on K has zero energy, hence vanishes), so quantifying over all such ρ
is faithful. The flat points are the points of S with two zero coordinates; the diagonal points are
the points of S with |x| = |y| = |z|. Proving `Claim` proves the conjecture; proving `¬ Claim` means
showing the density's minimum or maximum set is something else.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE069

open MeasureTheory

/-- Euclidean 3-space. -/
abbrev E3 : Type := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)

/-- The `i`-th coordinate. -/
noncomputable def coord (i : Fin 3) (x : E3) : ℝ := (EuclideanSpace.proj i : E3 →L[ℝ] ℝ) x

/-- `x⁴ + y⁴ + z⁴`. -/
noncomputable def quartic (x : E3) : ℝ := coord 0 x ^ 4 + coord 1 x ^ 4 + coord 2 x ^ 4

/-- The Fermat superball. -/
def K : Set E3 := {x | quartic x ≤ 1}

/-- Its boundary surface. -/
def S : Set E3 := {x | quartic x = 1}

/-- The six flat points. -/
def flatPts : Set E3 :=
  {y | y ∈ S ∧ ((coord 0 y = 0 ∧ coord 1 y = 0) ∨ (coord 0 y = 0 ∧ coord 2 y = 0) ∨
    (coord 1 y = 0 ∧ coord 2 y = 0))}

/-- The eight diagonal points `3^{-1/4}(±1,±1,±1)`. -/
def diagPts : Set E3 :=
  {y | y ∈ S ∧ |coord 0 y| = |coord 1 y| ∧ |coord 1 y| = |coord 2 y|}

/-- Surface measure on `S` (unnormalized 2-dimensional Hausdorff measure). -/
noncomputable def surf : Measure E3 := (Measure.hausdorffMeasure (2 : ℝ)).restrict S

/-- `ρ` is the (continuous) Newtonian equilibrium charge density of `K` w.r.t. `surf`. -/
def IsEquilibriumDensity (ρ : E3 → ℝ) : Prop :=
  Continuous ρ ∧ (∫ y, ρ y ∂surf) = 1 ∧
    ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ K, (∫ y, ρ y / ‖x - y‖ ∂surf) = c

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ ρ : E3 → ℝ, IsEquilibriumDensity ρ →
    (∀ p ∈ flatPts, ∀ y ∈ S, ρ p ≤ ρ y ∧ (ρ y ≤ ρ p → y ∈ flatPts)) ∧
    (∀ p ∈ diagPts, ∀ y ∈ S, ρ y ≤ ρ p ∧ (ρ p ≤ ρ y → y ∈ diagPts))

end OpenProblems.QEDE069
prov_reason: No literature on extremal points of the equilibrium density of superballs was found; the specific conjecture is QED's.

title: Fibonacci-modulated growing Jacobi matrix
credit: Extends Janas-Naboko (periodic modulations, e.g. arXiv:math/0605593) and Swiderski (arXiv:1707.06486) on periodically modulated Jacobi matrices.
plain: Take a Jacobi matrix with zero diagonal and off-diagonal weights sqrt(n). Double the weight at every position where the Fibonacci word has a 1. Periodic modulations of power-growing weights are known to produce spectral phase transitions. Determine the spectral type for this aperiodic modulation.
math: Let $f=f_1f_2f_3\cdots=0100101001001\cdots\in\{0,1\}^{\mathbb N}$ be the Fibonacci word, the fixed point of $0\mapsto01,\ 1\mapsto0$. Let $J$ be the Jacobi operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb N)$ with $(Ju)_n=a_{n-1}u_{n-1}+a_nu_{n+1}$, where $a_n=\sqrt n\,(1+f_n)$ and $a_0u_0:=0$. Since $\sum 1/a_n=\infty$, $J$ is self-adjoint (Carleman). Determine the spectral type of $J$. In particular: is $\sigma_{ac}(J)\neq\emptyset$? Is $\sigma_{ac}(J)=\mathbb R$? Is the spectrum on some interval pure point or singular continuous?

import Mathlib
/-! QED-E070: Fibonacci-modulated growing Jacobi matrix
Take the Jacobi matrix with zero diagonal and off-diagonal weights √n, and double the weight at every
position where the Fibonacci word has a 1. Determine the spectral type; the main question is whether
there is any absolutely continuous spectrum.
Informal statement: Let f = f₁f₂f₃⋯ = 0100101001001⋯ be the Fibonacci word, the fixed point of
0 ↦ 01, 1 ↦ 0. Let J be the Jacobi operator on ℓ²(ℕ) with (Ju)_n = a_{n−1}u_{n−1} + a_n u_{n+1},
a_n = √n (1 + f_n), a₀u₀ := 0. J is self-adjoint (Carleman). Determine the spectral type of J; in
particular, is σ_ac(J) ≠ ∅?
Formalization notes: `Claim` is the headline yes/no question σ_ac(J) ≠ ∅. Unbounded operators are
avoided via the standard correspondence: the spectral measure μ of J at δ₁ is the probability
measure on ℝ for which the generalized eigenfunctions P_n (P₀ = 0, P₁ = 1,
P_{n+1}(x) = (x P_n(x) − a_{n−1} P_{n−1}(x)) / a_n) are orthonormal in L²(μ). Since ∑ 1/a_n = ∞,
the moment problem is determinate, so μ is unique (it exists by Favard), and δ₁ is cyclic, so the
spectral type of J is that of μ. σ_ac(J) ≠ ∅ iff μ has a nonzero absolutely continuous part, i.e.
μ is not mutually singular with Lebesgue measure. The Fibonacci word is given by the standard
formula f_n = 2 + ⌊nφ⌋ − ⌊(n+1)φ⌋ (n ≥ 1), φ the golden ratio. Proving `Claim` shows σ_ac ≠ ∅;
proving `¬ Claim` shows the spectrum is purely singular. The finer questions (σ_ac = ℝ? pure point
or singular continuous on intervals?) are not part of `Claim`.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE070

open MeasureTheory

/-- The golden ratio. -/
noncomputable def phi : ℝ := (1 + Real.sqrt 5) / 2

/-- The `n`-th letter (n ≥ 1) of the Fibonacci word `0100101001001…`. -/
noncomputable def fibWord (n : ℕ) : ℤ := 2 + ⌊(n : ℝ) * phi⌋ - ⌊((n : ℝ) + 1) * phi⌋

/-- Off-diagonal weights `a_n = √n (1 + f_n)`. -/
noncomputable def a (n : ℕ) : ℝ := Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) * (1 + (fibWord n : ℝ))

/-- Generalized eigenfunctions: `P 0 = 0`, `P 1 = 1`, and the three-term recurrence. -/
noncomputable def P : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ
  | 0, _ => 0
  | 1, _ => 1
  | (n + 2), x => (x * P (n + 1) x - a n * P n x) / a (n + 1)

/-- `μ` is the spectral measure of `J` at `δ₁` (orthogonality measure of the `P n`, n ≥ 1). -/
def IsSpectralMeasure (μ : Measure ℝ) : Prop :=
  IsProbabilityMeasure μ ∧
    ∀ m n : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → 1 ≤ n →
      Integrable (fun x => P m x * P n x) μ ∧
        (∫ x, P m x * P n x ∂μ) = if m = n then (1 : ℝ) else 0

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ μ : Measure ℝ, IsSpectralMeasure μ → ¬ Measure.MutuallySingular μ volume

end OpenProblems.QEDE070
prov_reason: Transplants the Janas-Naboko-Swiderski theory of periodically modulated unbounded Jacobi weights to an aperiodic (Fibonacci) modulation; no source poses this case.

title: Maximal eigenfunction growth beyond surfaces of revolution
credit: C. D. Sogge and S. Zelditch, 'Focal points and sup-norms of eigenfunctions' (arXiv:1311.3999) and its two-dimensional addendum (arXiv:1409.2063, Rev. Mat. Iberoam. 2016).
plain: On the round sphere, some eigenfunctions are as peaked as theory allows, because every geodesic leaving the pole comes back to it. Sogge and Zelditch proved that on any real-analytic surface, maximally peaked eigenfunctions force such a 'pole'. Is rotational symmetry also forced: must such a surface be a surface of revolution?
math: Let $(M,g)$ be a compact connected boundaryless real-analytic Riemannian surface with $\Delta_g e_j=-\lambda_j^2e_j$, $\|e_j\|_{L^2}=1$. Say $g$ has maximal eigenfunction growth if $\limsup_j \|e_j\|_{L^\infty}/\lambda_j^{1/2}>0$ for some orthonormal eigenbasis. Decide whether every such $(M,g)$ carries a nontrivial isometric $S^1$-action, i.e. is a surface of revolution. (Necessary condition, Sogge-Zelditch 2016: $M$ has a pole $p$, meaning all geodesics from $p$ return smoothly closed at a common time $2T_p$.)

import Mathlib
/-! QED-E071: Maximal eigenfunction growth beyond surfaces of revolution
On the round sphere, some eigenfunctions are as peaked as theory allows, because every geodesic leaving the pole comes back to it. Sogge and Zelditch proved that on any real-analytic surface, maximally peaked eigenfunctions force such a 'pole'. Is rotational symmetry also forced: must such a surface be a surface of revolution?
Informal statement: Let (M,g) be a compact connected boundaryless real-analytic Riemannian surface with
Δ_g e_j = −λ_j² e_j, ‖e_j‖_{L²} = 1. Say g has maximal eigenfunction growth if
limsup_j ‖e_j‖_{L^∞} / λ_j^{1/2} > 0 for some orthonormal eigenbasis. Decide whether every such (M,g)
carries a nontrivial isometric S¹-action, i.e. is a surface of revolution. (Necessary condition,
Sogge–Zelditch 2016: M has a pole.)
Formalization notes: Model. By Nash's analytic embedding theorem (Nash 1966), every compact
real-analytic Riemannian manifold has a real-analytic isometric embedding into some ℝ^N; conversely
a compact real-analytic embedded surface with the induced metric is a compact real-analytic Riemannian
surface. All notions involved (eigenbases, sup norms, isometric circle actions) are isometry
invariant, so we quantify over compact connected real-analytic embedded surfaces M ⊂ ℝ^N (N ≥ 3) with
the induced metric. `IsAnalyticSurface`: locally M = {F = 0} for a real-analytic submersion
F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N−2} (no boundary; dimension 2 because N − 2 equations with surjective derivative; N ≥ 3
excludes degenerate cases such as N = 0, where a point would qualify). Riemannian measure: the
2-dimensional Hausdorff measure restricted to M (Mathlib's normalization differs from area by a
positive constant factor, which rescales L² norms and sup norms of normalized functions by a common
constant and does not affect eigenvalues, so the condition limsup > 0 is unchanged). Tangent plane:
`tangentConeAt ℝ M x`, which for an embedded C¹ submanifold is the tangent plane T_xM. Tangential
gradient: |∇_M f|²(x) = sup{(Df(x)v)² : v ∈ T_xM, |v| = 1}, and ⟨∇_M f, ∇_M g⟩ by polarization.
Eigenfunctions: smooth functions on M are exactly restrictions of smooth functions on ℝ^N (tubular
neighbourhood), and eigenfunctions are smooth (indeed analytic), so an eigenpair (λ, e) is an ambient
smooth e with ∫_M ⟨∇_M e, ∇_M φ⟩ = λ² ∫_M e φ for all ambient smooth φ (weak = strong for smooth e).
Real-valued bases suffice: for each eigenspace, sup over unit vectors of |u(x)| equals
(Σ_j |e_j(x)|²)^{1/2} for any (real or complex) orthonormal basis and is attained by a real vector.
Orthonormal eigenbasis: orthonormality in L²(M) and Parseval for all smooth φ (completeness). The
frequencies λ_j → ∞ along any enumeration, so limsup_j ‖e_j‖_∞/λ_j^{1/2} > 0 is "∃ c > 0 with
‖e_j‖_∞ ≥ c λ_j^{1/2} for infinitely many j" (`MaxGrowth`). Surface of revolution: a nontrivial
continuous action of S¹ = ℝ/ℤ (encoded as a 1-periodic ℝ-flow Φ on M) by isometries of the intrinsic
distance d_M (infimum of lengths, via `eVariationOn`, of paths in M); by Myers–Steenrod,
distance-preserving maps are smooth Riemannian isometries. A nontrivial continuous S¹ action has
finite kernel, so it induces an effective one. Connectedness is added (standard for this question).
Proving `Claim`: every such surface with maximal growth is a surface of revolution. Proving `¬Claim`:
a real-analytic surface with maximal growth but no isometric circle action (e.g. a non-rotational Zoll
surface with maximal growth).
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE071
noncomputable section

open MeasureTheory Filter Topology

/-- Ambient Euclidean space `ℝ^N`. -/
abbrev E (N : ℕ) : Type := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin N)

/-- `M ⊂ ℝ^N` is a compact connected real-analytic embedded surface without boundary. -/
def IsAnalyticSurface (N : ℕ) (M : Set (E N)) : Prop :=
  IsCompact M ∧ IsConnected M ∧
    ∀ x ∈ M, ∃ U : Set (E N), IsOpen U ∧ x ∈ U ∧
      ∃ F : E N → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (N - 2)),
        AnalyticOnNhd ℝ F U ∧ (∀ y ∈ U, Function.Surjective (fderiv ℝ F y)) ∧
          M ∩ U = {y : E N | y ∈ U ∧ F y = 0}

/-- Riemannian area measure of `M` (up to a constant factor): `𝓗²` restricted to `M`. -/
def area (N : ℕ) (M : Set (E N)) : Measure (E N) :=
  (Measure.hausdorffMeasure (2 : ℝ)).restrict M

/-- `|∇_M f|²(x)`: the squared norm of the tangential gradient. -/
def gradSq (N : ℕ) (M : Set (E N)) (f : E N → ℝ) (x : E N) : ℝ :=
  sSup ((fun v : E N => (fderiv ℝ f x v) ^ 2) '' {v : E N | v ∈ tangentConeAt ℝ M x ∧ ‖v‖ = 1})

/-- `⟨∇_M f, ∇_M g⟩(x)` by polarization. -/
def gradDot (N : ℕ) (M : Set (E N)) (f g : E N → ℝ) (x : E N) : ℝ :=
  (gradSq N M (f + g) x - gradSq N M (f - g) x) / 4

/-- Smooth functions on `ℝ^N` (their restrictions are exactly the smooth functions on `M`). -/
def IsSmooth (N : ℕ) (f : E N → ℝ) : Prop := ∀ k : ℕ, ContDiff ℝ k f

/-- `Δ_M e = −lam² e`, weakly against all smooth test functions. -/
def IsEigen (N : ℕ) (M : Set (E N)) (lam : ℝ) (e : E N → ℝ) : Prop :=
  IsSmooth N e ∧ ∀ φ : E N → ℝ, IsSmooth N φ →
    ∫ x, gradDot N M e φ x ∂(area N M) = lam ^ 2 * ∫ x, e x * φ x ∂(area N M)

/-- An orthonormal eigenbasis `(e_j)` of `L²(M)` with frequencies `lam_j ≥ 0`. -/
def IsEigenbasis (N : ℕ) (M : Set (E N)) (lam : ℕ → ℝ) (e : ℕ → E N → ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ j : ℕ, 0 ≤ lam j ∧ IsEigen N M (lam j) (e j)) ∧
    (∀ i j : ℕ, ∫ x, e i x * e j x ∂(area N M) = if i = j then (1 : ℝ) else 0) ∧
    ∀ φ : E N → ℝ, IsSmooth N φ →
      HasSum (fun j : ℕ => (∫ x, e j x * φ x ∂(area N M)) ^ 2) (∫ x, φ x ^ 2 ∂(area N M))

/-- Sup norm on `M`. -/
def supNorm (N : ℕ) (M : Set (E N)) (f : E N → ℝ) : ℝ := sSup ((fun x : E N => |f x|) '' M)

/-- Maximal eigenfunction growth: `limsup_j ‖e_j‖_∞ / lam_j^{1/2} > 0` for some eigenbasis. -/
def MaxGrowth (N : ℕ) (M : Set (E N)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (lam : ℕ → ℝ) (e : ℕ → E N → ℝ), IsEigenbasis N M lam e ∧
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ J : ℕ, ∃ j : ℕ, J ≤ j ∧ c * Real.sqrt (lam j) ≤ supNorm N M (e j)

/-- Intrinsic (path-length) distance on `M`. -/
def dist_M (N : ℕ) (M : Set (E N)) (x y : E N) : ENNReal :=
  ⨅ (γ : ℝ → E N) (_ : ContinuousOn γ (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) ∧ γ 0 = x ∧ γ 1 = y ∧
      ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, γ t ∈ M),
    eVariationOn γ (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)

/-- `M` carries a nontrivial continuous isometric action of the circle `ℝ/ℤ`. -/
def HasCircleAction (N : ℕ) (M : Set (E N)) : Prop :=
  ∃ Φ : ℝ → E N → E N,
    (∀ t : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ M, Φ t x ∈ M) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ M, Φ 0 x = x) ∧
    (∀ s t : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ M, Φ (s + t) x = Φ s (Φ t x)) ∧
    (∀ t : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ M, Φ (t + 1) x = Φ t x) ∧
    ContinuousOn (fun q : ℝ × E N => Φ q.1 q.2) (Set.univ ×ˢ M) ∧
    (∀ t : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ M, ∀ y ∈ M, dist_M N M (Φ t x) (Φ t y) = dist_M N M x y) ∧
    ∃ t : ℝ, ∃ x ∈ M, Φ t x ≠ x

/-- Every compact real-analytic surface with maximal eigenfunction growth is a surface of
revolution. -/
def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ N : ℕ, 3 ≤ N → ∀ M : Set (E N), IsAnalyticSurface N M → MaxGrowth N M → HasCircleAction N M

end
end OpenProblems.QEDE071

Friedrichs extension. Dirichlet form: `dform u v = Σ_faces ∫ (conj ∂₁u ∂₁v + conj ∂₂u ∂₂v)` with

`S = ∂[0,1]³ ⊂ ℝ³`. Each face is the image of the closed unit square under an affine isometric chart;
since all faces sit inside the same `ℝ³`, the edge identifications are those of the cube and
continuity on `S` is exactly "matching edge traces". -/

/-- Points of `ℝ³`. -/
abbrev P3 : Type := Fin 3 → ℝ

/-- The six faces: `(i, b)` is the face `{x ∈ [0,1]³ | x i = b}` (`false ↦ 0`, `true ↦ 1`). -/
abbrev Face : Type := Fin 3 × Bool

/-- The fixed coordinate value of a face. -/
def bval (b : Bool) : ℝ := if b then 1 else 0

/-- Isometric affine chart of face `(i, b)`: `(s, t) ↦ x` with `x i = b`, `x (i+1) = s`, `x (i+2) = t`
(indices mod 3). -/
def chart (f : Face) (p : ℝ × ℝ) : P3 := fun m : Fin 3 =>
  if m = f.1 then bval f.2 else if m = f.1 + 1 then p.1 else p.2

/-- The closed unit square. -/
def cSq : Set (ℝ × ℝ) := Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ×ˢ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1

/-- The open unit square (faces are integrated over it; the boundary is Lebesgue-null). -/
def Sq : Set (ℝ × ℝ) := Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 ×ˢ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1

/-- The cube surface `S = ∂[0,1]³`. -/
def S : Set P3 := ⋃ f : Face, chart f '' cSq

/-- Pull-back of a function on `ℝ³` to face `f`'s square. -/
def pull (u : P3 → ℂ) (f : Face) : ℝ × ℝ → ℂ := fun p => u (chart f p)

/-- Partial derivative in the first square coordinate. -/
def d1 (v : ℝ × ℝ → ℂ) (p : ℝ × ℝ) : ℂ := deriv (fun s : ℝ => v (s, p.2)) p.1

/-- Partial derivative in the second square coordinate. -/
def d2 (v : ℝ × ℝ → ℂ) (p : ℝ × ℝ) : ℂ := deriv (fun t : ℝ => v (p.1, t)) p.2

/-- Core of the Dirichlet form: functions continuous on `S` whose restriction to every closed face
is the restriction of a `C^∞` function on `ℝ²` (smooth up to the edges). -/
def IsTest (u : P3 → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ContinuousOn u S ∧
    ∀ f : Face, ∃ g : ℝ × ℝ → ℂ, (∀ k : ℕ, ContDiff ℝ k g) ∧ Set.EqOn (pull u f) g cSq

/-- `u` is (a representative of) an element of `L²(S)` for the surface (area) measure. -/
def IsL2 (u : P3 → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : Face, AEStronglyMeasurable (pull u f) (volume.restrict Sq) ∧
    Integrable (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => ‖pull u f p‖ ^ 2) (volume.restrict Sq)

/-- `L²(S)` inner product, conjugate-linear in the first slot. -/
def ip (u v : P3 → ℂ) : ℂ :=
  ∑ f : Face, ∫ p in Sq, (starRingEnd ℂ) (pull u f p) * pull v f p

/-- `‖u‖²_{L²(S)}` (the mass). -/
def normSq (u : P3 → ℂ) : ℝ := ∑ f : Face, ∫ p in Sq, ‖pull u f p‖ ^ 2

/-- Sesquilinear Dirichlet form `E(u,v) = ∫_S ⟨∇u, ∇v⟩`, computed face by face. -/
def dform (u v : P3 → ℂ) : ℂ :=
  ∑ f : Face, ∫ p in Sq,
    ((starRingEnd ℂ) (d1 (pull u f) p) * d1 (pull v f) p +
      (starRingEnd ℂ) (d2 (pull u f) p) * d2 (pull v f) p)

/-- Energy `E(u) = ∫_S |∇u|²`. -/
def energy (u : P3 → ℂ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ f : Face, ∫ p in Sq, (‖d1 (pull u f) p‖ ^ 2 + ‖d2 (pull u f) p‖ ^ 2)

/-- `w` is a sequence in the core that converges to `e` in `L²` and is Cauchy for the energy, i.e.
it witnesses that `e` lies in the form domain `H¹(S)` (closure of the core in the form norm). -/
def Approximates (e : P3 → ℂ) (w : ℕ → P3 → ℂ) : Prop :=
  (∀ m : ℕ, IsTest (w m)) ∧
    Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => normSq (w m - e)) atTop (𝓝 0) ∧
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ m l : ℕ, N ≤ m → N ≤ l → energy (w m - w l) < ε

/-- `e` is an eigenfunction of the Friedrichs Laplacian `A = -Δ ≥ 0` with eigenvalue `lam`:
`e ∈ H¹(S)` and `E(e, φ) = lam ⟨e, φ⟩` for every `φ` in the core. -/
def IsEigenpair (lam : ℝ) (e : P3 → ℂ) : Prop :=
  IsL2 e ∧ ∃ w : ℕ → P3 → ℂ, Approximates e w ∧
    ∀ φ : P3 → ℂ, IsTest φ →
      Tendsto (fun m : ℕ => dform (w m) φ) atTop (𝓝 ((lam : ℂ) * ip e φ))

/-- An orthonormal eigenbasis of `L²(S)` for the Friedrichs Laplacian (eigenvalues of `-Δ`,
listed with multiplicity in any order). Completeness is Parseval's identity on the dense core. -/
def IsEigenbasis (lam : ℕ → ℝ) (e : ℕ → P3 → ℂ) : Prop :=
  (∀ n : ℕ, IsEigenpair (lam n) (e n)) ∧
    (∀ n m : ℕ, ip (e n) (e m) = if n = m then (1 : ℂ) else 0) ∧
    ∀ u : P3 → ℂ, IsTest u → HasSum (fun n : ℕ => ‖ip (e n) u‖ ^ 2) (normSq u)

/-- Some eigenvalue of the Friedrichs Laplacian of the cube surface is not a rational multiple
of `π²`. -/
def Claim : Prop :=
  ∃ (lam : ℝ) (e : P3 → ℂ), IsEigenpair lam e ∧ 0 < normSq e ∧
    ∀ q : ℚ, lam ≠ Real.pi ^ 2 * (q : ℝ)

end
end OpenProblems.QEDE072
prov_reason: The numerical study arXiv:1809.09909 splits cube eigenfunctions into torus-type and singular ones but does not pose non-arithmeticity; the reviewer found no source stating the question.

title: Spikes at the primes
credit: C. R. de Oliveira and G. Q. Pellegrino, '(De)Localization in the Prime Schrodinger Operator', 2001, arXiv:cond-mat/0103313.
plain: Put a bump of fixed height at every prime on the half-line lattice and study the electron (discrete Schrodinger operator). What kind of spectrum does it have inside the free band (-2,2)? If the primes behaved like a random sparse set (Cramer model), the states would be localized (pure point spectrum); is that true for the actual primes?
math: Let $(Hu)(n)=u(n+1)+u(n-1)+\lambda\mathbf 1_{\mathbb P}(n)u(n)$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb N)$ with Dirichlet condition $u(0)=0$, $\lambda\ne0$. Determine the spectral type of $H$ on $(-2,2)$. In particular: is the spectral measure restricted to $(-2,2)$ pure point (with exponentially or sub-exponentially decaying eigenfunctions), or does it have a singular continuous part, e.g. near $E=0$?
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-E073: Spikes at the primes
Put a potential spike of fixed height λ ≠ 0 at every prime on the half-line lattice. Inside the free
band (−2, 2), is the spectrum pure point (as for a random sparse set of the same density), or is there
a singular continuous component?
Informal statement: Let (Hu)(n) = u(n+1) + u(n−1) + λ 1_ℙ(n) u(n) on ℓ²(ℕ) with Dirichlet condition
u(0) = 0, λ ≠ 0. Determine the spectral type of H on (−2, 2). In particular: is the spectral measure
restricted to (−2, 2) pure point, or does it have a singular continuous part?
Formalization notes: `Claim` is the sharpest yes/no form: for every λ ≠ 0, the spectral measure of H
restricted to (−2, 2) is pure point. H is a bounded Jacobi operator (a_n = 1, b_n = λ 1_ℙ(n)), δ₁ is
cyclic, and its spectral measure μ is the unique probability measure making the generalized
eigenfunctions P_n orthonormal (P₀ = 0, P₁ = 1, P_{n+1}(x) = (x − λ 1_ℙ(n)) P_n(x) − P_{n−1}(x)).
Pure point on (−2, 2) means μ((−2,2) \ C) = 0 for some countable set C. Absolutely continuous
spectrum is already excluded (Remling 2011, since 1_ℙ is not eventually periodic), so `¬ Claim`
means: for some λ ≠ 0 there is singular continuous spectrum in (−2, 2). Eigenfunction decay rates
are not part of `Claim`. The literature numerics (de Oliveira–Pellegrino 2001) suggest delocalized
states near E = 0, i.e. that `¬ Claim` may hold.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE073

open MeasureTheory

/-- The potential `λ · 1_ℙ(n)`. -/
noncomputable def V (lam : ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ := Set.indicator {p : ℕ | Nat.Prime p} (fun _ => lam) n

/-- Generalized eigenfunctions of `H` (Dirichlet at 0). -/
noncomputable def P (lam : ℝ) : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ
  | 0, _ => 0
  | 1, _ => 1
  | (n + 2), x => (x - V lam (n + 1)) * P lam (n + 1) x - P lam n x

/-- `μ` is the spectral measure of `H` at `δ₁`. -/
def IsSpectralMeasure (lam : ℝ) (μ : Measure ℝ) : Prop :=
  IsProbabilityMeasure μ ∧
    ∀ m n : ℕ, 1 ≤ m → 1 ≤ n →
      Integrable (fun x => P lam m x * P lam n x) μ ∧
        (∫ x, P lam m x * P lam n x ∂μ) = if m = n then (1 : ℝ) else 0

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ lam : ℝ, lam ≠ 0 → ∀ μ : Measure ℝ, IsSpectralMeasure lam μ →
    ∃ C : Set ℝ, C.Countable ∧ μ (Set.Ioo (-2 : ℝ) 2 \ C) = 0

end OpenProblems.QEDE073
prov_reason: The spectral type of the discrete Schrodinger operator with potential supported on the primes is posed (and studied numerically) in the literature, as the notes say.

title: Two-frequency localization
credit: Recognised open problem from the Bourgain-Goldstein / Bourgain-Goldstein-Schlag multi-frequency programme; stated open in arXiv:2603.07180 (2026). Pure point spectrum without exponential decay at fixed Diophantine frequency: Eliasson, Acta Math. 1997.
premise_risks: arXiv:2603.07180 (2026 preprint): the problem relies on its statement that it is unknown whether any fixed Diophantine frequency vector gives localization.
arXiv:2603.10649 (2026 preprint): cited background; content not relied on in the statement.
plain: Take a one-dimensional lattice Schrödinger operator whose potential is the sum of two cosines with frequencies √2 and √3, and make the coupling strong. Prove that for these specific frequencies, not just for almost every frequency pair, almost every phase gives localized eigenfunctions that decay exponentially.
math: For $\lambda>0$ and $\theta\in\mathbb T^2$ let $(H_{\lambda,\theta}\psi)(n)=\psi(n+1)+\psi(n-1)+\lambda\big(\cos2\pi(n\sqrt2+\theta_1)+\cos2\pi(n\sqrt3+\theta_2)\big)\psi(n)$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb Z)$. Prove there is $\lambda_0$ such that for all $\lambda\ge\lambda_0$ and Lebesgue-a.e. $\theta$, $H_{\lambda,\theta}$ has pure point spectrum with exponentially decaying eigenfunctions (Anderson localization).
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-E074: Two-frequency localization
For the lattice Schrödinger operator on ℤ with potential λ(cos 2π(n√2+θ₁) + cos 2π(n√3+θ₂)), prove that for all large λ and almost every phase θ the operator has pure point spectrum with exponentially decaying eigenfunctions, for this specific frequency vector.
Informal statement: For $\lambda>0$ and $\theta\in\mathbb T^2$ let $(H_{\lambda,\theta}\psi)(n)=\psi(n+1)+\psi(n-1)+\lambda\big(\cos2\pi(n\sqrt2+\theta_1)+\cos2\pi(n\sqrt3+\theta_2)\big)\psi(n)$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb Z)$. Prove there is $\lambda_0$ such that for all $\lambda\ge\lambda_0$ and Lebesgue-a.e. $\theta$, $H_{\lambda,\theta}$ has pure point spectrum with exponentially decaying eigenfunctions (Anderson localization).
Formalization notes: Anderson localization (pure point spectrum with exponentially decaying eigenfunctions) is encoded as the existence of a real orthonormal basis of ℓ²(ℤ) consisting of exponentially decaying eigenfunctions; for a bounded self-adjoint operator, pure point spectrum is equivalent to the eigenvectors being complete. Real eigenfunctions suffice since H is a real symmetric operator. Any ONB of ℓ²(ℤ) is countably infinite, so ℕ-indexing loses nothing. Orthonormality uses tsum, legitimate because exponential decay makes the products summable; completeness is Parseval's identity. θ ranges over ℝ² with Lebesgue measure; the potential is ℤ²-periodic in θ, so a.e. on ℝ² is the same as a.e. on the torus. Proving ¬Claim means: for arbitrarily large λ a positive-measure set of phases fails localization.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE074

/-- The quasi-periodic potential `λ (cos 2π(n√2 + θ₁) + cos 2π(n√3 + θ₂))`. -/
noncomputable def pot (lam : ℝ) (θ : ℝ × ℝ) (n : ℤ) : ℝ :=
  lam * (Real.cos (2 * Real.pi * ((n : ℝ) * Real.sqrt 2 + θ.1)) +
    Real.cos (2 * Real.pi * ((n : ℝ) * Real.sqrt 3 + θ.2)))

/-- `ψ` solves `H_{λ,θ} ψ = E ψ` pointwise. -/
def IsEigenfunction (lam : ℝ) (θ : ℝ × ℝ) (E : ℝ) (ψ : ℤ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℤ, ψ (n + 1) + ψ (n - 1) + pot lam θ n * ψ n = E * ψ n

/-- `ψ` decays exponentially. -/
def ExpDecaying (ψ : ℤ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ C c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ n : ℤ, |ψ n| ≤ C * Real.exp (-(c * |(n : ℝ)|))

/-- Anderson localization: `ℓ²(ℤ)` has an orthonormal basis `(ψ k)` of exponentially decaying
eigenfunctions of `H_{λ,θ}` (orthonormality plus Parseval's identity for every `ℓ²` vector). -/
def AndersonLocalized (lam : ℝ) (θ : ℝ × ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (ψ : ℕ → ℤ → ℝ) (E : ℕ → ℝ),
    (∀ k : ℕ, IsEigenfunction lam θ (E k) (ψ k) ∧ ExpDecaying (ψ k)) ∧
    (∀ k j : ℕ, ∑' n : ℤ, ψ k n * ψ j n = if k = j then (1 : ℝ) else 0) ∧
    (∀ φ : ℤ → ℝ, Summable (fun n : ℤ => φ n ^ 2) →
      HasSum (fun k : ℕ => (∑' n : ℤ, φ n * ψ k n) ^ 2) (∑' n : ℤ, φ n ^ 2))

/-- Large-coupling Anderson localization for a.e. phase, at the fixed frequency vector `(√2, √3)`. -/
def Claim : Prop :=
  ∃ lam₀ : ℝ, ∀ lam : ℝ, lam₀ ≤ lam →
    ∀ᶠ θ in MeasureTheory.ae (MeasureTheory.volume : MeasureTheory.Measure (ℝ × ℝ)),
      AndersonLocalized lam θ

end OpenProblems.QEDE074
prov_reason: Fixed-frequency large-coupling localization for multi-frequency quasi-periodic operators is a recognised open problem (stated as unknown in arXiv:2603.07180); this is an explicit instance.

title: Wind-driven fire confinement threshold
credit: A. Bressan, Differential inclusions and the control of forest fires, J. Differential Equations 2007 (non-isotropic Thm 5)
results: sigma*(a,b) >= Lambda*(a-b), Lambda ~ 1.62621 (isotropic lower bound, arXiv 2610.36919, Thm 4.1). Proof: F contains the disc of radius a-b. Bressan's comparison lemma moves blocking from F to that disc, and rescaling time reduces to unit speed. sigma*(a,b) <= 2 max_{theta in [0,pi]} (a+b cos theta) sin theta (Bressan, Thm 5, non-isotropic case; applies because rho is even and nonincreasing on [0,pi]). This equals 2a at b=0 and tends to (3 sqrt3/2) a as b->a.
premise_risks: arXiv:2610.36919 (2026 preprint): isotropic lower bound Lambda ~ 1.6262 (Thm 4.1), used for the lower bound recorded in the notes.
plain: A fire spreads from a point, faster downwind: speed a + b cos(theta) in direction theta (0<=b<a). Firefighters build a barrier at speed sigma. Let sigma*(a,b) be the smallest speed that can confine the fire. Known: 1.626(a-b) <= sigma* <= 2 max (a+b cos theta) sin theta. Improve either bound, especially in the strong-wind limit b/a -> 1, where the lower bound tends to 0 but the upper bound stays near 2.6a.
math: With F_b = conv{r e^{i theta}: 0<=r<=1+b cos theta}, R_0 the open unit disc and Bressan-admissible barriers, prove that for some fixed b in (0,1) the fire can be confined with some sigma < 2 max_theta (1+b cos theta) sin theta, i.e. Bressan's anisotropic upper bound is not sharp.
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-E075: Wind-driven fire confinement threshold
A fire spreads from a bounded region with speed 1 + b cos θ in direction θ (0 ≤ b < 1, wind along the
positive x-axis); firefighters build barriers at speed σ (total length ≤ σt at time t). Bressan's
non-isotropic construction confines the fire whenever σ > U(b) := 2 max_θ (1 + b cos θ) sin θ.
Can one do strictly better for some wind strength?
Informal statement: (corrected) With F_b = conv{r e^{iθ} : 0 ≤ r ≤ 1 + b cos θ}, R₀ the open unit disc
and Bressan-admissible barriers (rectifiable, increasing, H¹(γ(t)) ≤ σt), show that for some fixed
b ∈ (0,1) some σ < 2 max_θ (1 + b cos θ) sin θ confines the fire (i.e. Bressan's upper bound is not
sharp for some fixed wind ratio). The original target "liminf_{b→a} σ*(a,b)/a > 0" is trivially true:
conv F contains the disc of radius ρ = min_u h_F(u) about 0, which equals a²/(4b) for b ≥ a/2, so
the comparison argument already gives σ* ≥ Λ·a²/(4b) → Λa/4 > 0.
Formalization notes: Scaling a = 1 loses nothing (σ*(a,b) = aσ*(1,b/a)). The plane is ℂ (Euclidean
metric, so `hausdorffMeasure 1` is length). R₀ is the open unit disc (with R₀ = {0} a single point
barrier at the origin would trivially block everything; the threshold does not depend on the bounded
open R₀). A barrier strategy γ is admissible at speed σ if it is increasing in t, each γ(t) is empty
or a countable union of Lipschitz images of [0,1] (Bressan's rectifiability condition), and
H¹(γ(t)) ≤ σt. Burned points at time t are x(t) for Lipschitz paths with |x(0)| < 1, ẋ(s) ∈ F_b
a.e. on [0,t] (Lipschitz paths are a.e. differentiable; any absolutely continuous path with
ẋ ∈ F_b is Lipschitz), and x(s) ∉ γ(s) for s ∈ [0,t]. Confinement: all burned points stay in a fixed
ball. Known: Λ·ρ(b) ≤ σ*(1,b) ≤ U(b), Λ ≈ 1.6262 (isotropic lower bound).
Proving `Claim` = exhibiting b ∈ (0,1) and a confining strategy of speed σ < U(b).
Proving `¬Claim` = Bressan's anisotropic construction is optimal for every b ∈ (0,1).
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE075
noncomputable section

/-- Convexified spreading set for wind strength `b` (unit base speed). -/
def Fset (b : ℝ) : Set ℂ :=
  convexHull ℝ {z : ℂ | ∃ r θ : ℝ, 0 ≤ r ∧ r ≤ 1 + b * Real.cos θ ∧
    z = (r : ℂ) * Complex.exp ((θ : ℂ) * Complex.I)}

/-- Bressan-admissible barrier strategy of construction speed `σ`. -/
def Admissible (σ : ℝ) (γ : ℝ → Set ℂ) : Prop :=
  (∀ s t : ℝ, 0 ≤ s → s ≤ t → γ s ⊆ γ t) ∧
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure (1 : ℝ) (γ t) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (σ * t)) ∧
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → γ t = ∅ ∨
    ∃ c : ℕ → ℝ → ℂ, (∀ m : ℕ, ∃ K : NNReal, LipschitzWith K (c m)) ∧
      γ t = ⋃ m : ℕ, c m '' Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)

/-- `z` is burned at time `t` (reached by an admissible fire path avoiding the barrier). -/
def Burned (b : ℝ) (γ : ℝ → Set ℂ) (t : ℝ) (z : ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ x : ℝ → ℂ, (∃ K : NNReal, LipschitzWith K x) ∧ ‖x 0‖ < 1 ∧ x t = z ∧
    (∀ᵐ s ∂MeasureTheory.volume, s ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) t → ∀ v : ℂ, HasDerivAt x v s → v ∈ Fset b) ∧
    ∀ s ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) t, x s ∉ γ s

/-- Speed `σ` suffices to confine the fire with wind `b`. -/
def Confines (b σ : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ γ : ℝ → Set ℂ, Admissible σ γ ∧ ∃ M : ℝ, ∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → ∀ z : ℂ, Burned b γ t z → ‖z‖ ≤ M

/-- Bressan's upper bound `2 max_θ (1 + b cos θ) sin θ`. -/
noncomputable def U (b : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  2 * sSup (Set.range fun θ : ℝ => (1 + b * Real.cos θ) * Real.sin θ)

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∃ b : ℝ, 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧ ∃ σ : ℝ, σ < U b ∧ Confines b σ

end

end OpenProblems.QEDE075
M_fix_reason: The original main target liminf_{b->a} sigma*(a,b)/a > 0 is trivially true. Since F is convexified, conv F contains the disc of radius rho = min_u h_F(u) about 0, and rho = a^2/(4b) for b >= a/2 (at b=a, rho = a/4). The same comparison argument that gives Lambda(a-b) then gives sigma* >= Lambda a^2/(4b) -> Lambda a/4 > 0. Also R_0 = {0} is degenerate, because a single point barrier at the origin blocks everything; it was replaced by the unit disc.
prov_reason: This is an anisotropic (wind-driven) version of Bressan's fire confinement problem; the bounds were derived by QED.

title: Blank jigsaw with few edge shapes
credit: Mossel & Ross (shotgun assembly); Bordenave, Feige, Mossel 2016, arXiv:1605.03086; Nenadov, Pfister, Steger 2017, arXiv:1701.04813
plain: A jigsaw with no picture can only be solved from the shapes of its pieces. Each internal edge is one of k shapes (a tab that fits only its own matching blank), and pieces may be turned. How small can k be if some n×n blank jigsaw still goes together in exactly one way? Counting shows k must be at least about √n, and random puzzles need about n.
math: An $n\times n$ jigsaw with $k$ edge types is a map assigning to each internal edge of the $n\times n$ grid a type in $[k]$ and an orientation (which side carries the tab); border edges are flat. Its pieces are the $n^2$ unit squares, each regarded as a distinct physical object carrying its four (type, tab/blank) labels up to rotation. An assembly is a placement of all pieces bijectively on the cells, each rotated by a multiple of $90^\circ$, so that every internal edge joins a tab and a blank of the same type and all flat edges lie on the border. Let $k(n)$ be the least $k$ for which some $n\times n$ jigsaw with $k$ edge types has exactly one assembly up to the four rotations of the whole square. Determine the order of $k(n)$; in particular, is $k(n)=\Theta(\sqrt n)$?
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-E076: Blank jigsaw with few edge shapes
A blank n×n jigsaw has each internal edge cut in one of k shapes (a tab fitting only its own blank);
pieces may be rotated. How small can k be if some n×n blank jigsaw still assembles in exactly one way
(up to rotating the whole square)? Counting gives k ≥ c√n; random puzzles need about n.
Informal statement: An n×n jigsaw with k edge types assigns to each internal edge of the n×n grid a type
in [k] and an orientation (which side carries the tab); border edges are flat. Pieces are the n² unit
squares, each a distinct physical object carrying its four (type, tab/blank) labels up to rotation. An
assembly places all pieces bijectively on the cells, each rotated by a multiple of 90°, so that every
internal edge joins a tab and a blank of the same type and all flat edges lie on the border. Let k(n)
be the least k for which some n×n jigsaw with k edge types has exactly one assembly up to the four
rotations of the whole square. Is k(n) = Θ(√n)? Since k(n) ≥ c√n is known (unique assembly forces
all n² pieces to be distinct), Claim is the upper bound k(n) = O(√n).
Formalization notes: Cells are `Fin n × Fin n` (row, column; row 0 on top). Sides are `Fin 4` in
clockwise order 0 = N, 1 = E, 2 = S, 3 = W. A side label is `none` (flat) or `some (t, b)` with type
`t : Fin k` and `b = true` for a tab. `Valid L`: flat exactly on the border, and horizontally /
vertically adjacent cells show the same type with opposite tab/blank. A jigsaw is a valid labelling
`side` of the solved grid; piece p is cell p of the solved grid. An assembly is `(σ, r)`: piece p goes
to cell σ p rotated clockwise r p quarter-turns, so cell c shows on side d the label
`side (σ⁻¹ c) (d − r (σ⁻¹ c))`. Rotating a valid assembly as a whole gives a valid assembly with every
r increased by 1, so the four global rotations of the solved assembly are always 4 distinct
assemblies; "exactly one assembly up to rotation" ⇔ the number of valid assemblies is exactly 4.
Proving `Claim` = ∃ C, ∀ n ≥ 1, a uniquely assembling n×n jigsaw with ≤ C√n edge types.
Proving `¬Claim` = k(n)/√n is unbounded.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE076

/-- Cells of the n×n grid. -/
abbrev Cell (n : ℕ) : Type := Fin n × Fin n

/-- Side label: flat (`none`) or (type, is-tab). -/
abbrev Label (k : ℕ) : Type := Option (Fin k × Bool)

/-- Two sides fit: same type, one tab and one blank. -/
def Fits {k : ℕ} (x y : Label k) : Prop :=
  ∃ t : Fin k, ∃ b : Bool, x = some (t, b) ∧ y = some (t, !b)

/-- Side `d` of cell `c` is on the outer border. -/
def OnBorder {n : ℕ} (c : Cell n) (d : Fin 4) : Prop :=
  (d = 0 ∧ (c.1 : ℕ) = 0) ∨ (d = 1 ∧ (c.2 : ℕ) + 1 = n) ∨
  (d = 2 ∧ (c.1 : ℕ) + 1 = n) ∨ (d = 3 ∧ (c.2 : ℕ) = 0)

/-- A labelling of the sides of all cells is a correctly fitted puzzle. -/
def Valid {n k : ℕ} (L : Cell n → Fin 4 → Label k) : Prop :=
  (∀ (c : Cell n) (d : Fin 4), L c d = none ↔ OnBorder c d) ∧
  (∀ c c' : Cell n, c.1 = c'.1 → (c.2 : ℕ) + 1 = (c'.2 : ℕ) → Fits (L c 1) (L c' 3)) ∧
  (∀ c c' : Cell n, c.2 = c'.2 → (c.1 : ℕ) + 1 = (c'.1 : ℕ) → Fits (L c 2) (L c' 0))

/-- Labels shown on the grid when piece `p` is put at cell `σ p`, rotated by `r p` quarter-turns. -/
def placed {n k : ℕ} (side : Cell n → Fin 4 → Label k)
    (a : Equiv.Perm (Cell n) × (Cell n → Fin 4)) : Cell n → Fin 4 → Label k :=
  fun c d => side (a.1.symm c) (d - a.2 (a.1.symm c))

/-- Number of valid assemblies of the jigsaw `side`. -/
noncomputable def numAssemblies {n k : ℕ} (side : Cell n → Fin 4 → Label k) : ℕ :=
  Nat.card {a : Equiv.Perm (Cell n) × (Cell n → Fin 4) // Valid (placed side a)}

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → ∃ k : ℕ, (k : ℝ) ≤ C * Real.sqrt (n : ℝ) ∧
    ∃ side : Cell n → Fin 4 → Label k, Valid side ∧ numAssemblies side = 4

end OpenProblems.QEDE076
prov_reason: This is a deterministic-design version of the random jigsaw unique-reconstruction thresholds; the searches found no source posing the designed minimum k(n).

title: Critical linear firefighter rate on Z^3
credit: Extension of Develin-Hartke (arXiv:math/0409195) and Dyer-Martinez-Pedroza-Thorne (arXiv:1507.03050, Cor. 4); o(t) failure from arXiv:2002.11205.
results: c* >= 8/243 (~0.033), elementary: Loomis-Whitney gives |vertex boundary of B| >= |B|^{2/3}; for c<2a^2-6a^3 with a=2/9, a large initial cube burns forever by induction b_t >= (a(t+T0))^3. Using the asymptotically sharp Wang-Wang vertex isoperimetry (l1-balls, constant 4(3/4)^{2/3}) the same argument heuristically gives ~32/27, not checked rigorously c* <= 8, elementary: protect the l1-sphere |x|_1=D (4D^2+2 vertices) before step D-R; c>8 suffices for large D.
plain: On the 3D grid, a finite fire spreads to all unprotected neighbours each step, and at step t you may protect about ct new vertices. It is known that linear growth is the right order. Elementary arguments show that rate c>8 always contains the fire and that c<32/27 does not. Narrow this gap, or find the exact critical rate.
math: Let c* = inf{c : for every finite initial fire B_0 ⊂ Z^3 there is a protection schedule with at most ⌊ct⌋ newly protected vertices at step t that keeps the total burnt set finite}. Elementary: the growth recursion |B_{t+1}| ≥ |B_t| + |∂B_t| − c(t+1)(t+2)/2 with the Wang–Wang vertex-isoperimetric inequality in Z^3 gives c* ≥ 32/27; numerics suggest a static wall gives c* ≲ 6.4. Target: prove c* > 32/27, i.e. some rate c > 32/27 fails to contain some finite outbreak.
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-E077: Critical linear firefighter rate on Z^3
On Z^3 a finite fire spreads each step to all unprotected neighbours, and at step t one may protect about ct new vertices. Linear rate is the right order; the question is the critical constant c*. This file asks to improve the stated lower bound.
Informal statement: Let c* = inf{c : for every finite initial fire B_0 ⊂ Z^3 there is a protection schedule with at most ⌊c t⌋ newly protected vertices at step t that keeps the total burnt set finite}. Known (QED-derived, elementary): 8/243 ≤ c* ≤ 8 (bound field and W); M additionally records 64/243 ≤ c* ≤ 48/7 (not independently checked here; numerics suggest a static ℓ^4-ball wall gives ≈ 6.4). Target: prove c* > 32/27, i.e. some rate c > 32/27 fails to contain some finite outbreak.
Note: c* ≥ 32/27 already follows from the growth recursion |B_{t+1}| ≥ |B_t| + |∂B_t| − c(t+1)(t+2)/2 together with the
Wang–Wang vertex-isoperimetric inequality in Z^3 (|∂A| ≳ 4(3|A|/4)^{2/3}); the 64/243 bound is the same argument with the
Loomis–Whitney constant |∂A| ≥ 2|A|^{2/3}. So 64/243 is not a meaningful target.
Formalization notes: Fire dynamics: step t+1 = protect P(t+1), then spread to unprotected neighbours; protected vertices stay protected forever; protecting an already burnt vertex is allowed but useless, and re-protecting wastes budget, so allowing arbitrary sets of size ≤ c·s is equivalent to the usual rules. The fire is deterministic, so adaptive strategies are the same as fixed schedules P : ℕ → Finset V3. Budget at step 0 is 0. Containment = the union of all burnt sets is finite (equivalently, the fire stops). Contains is monotone in c, so c* > 32/27 ⇔ ∃ c > 32/27, ¬Contains c. The lower bound is the formalized side because the upper side is essentially settled numerically (≈6.4 wall). Proving ¬Claim means every rate c > 32/27 contains all finite outbreaks, i.e. c* ≤ 32/27 (hence = 32/27).
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE077

/-- The vertices of the grid `Z^3`. -/
abbrev V3 : Type := ℤ × ℤ × ℤ

/-- Grid adjacency: `ℓ¹` distance exactly `1`. -/
def Adj3 (u v : V3) : Prop :=
  |u.1 - v.1| + |u.2.1 - v.2.1| + |u.2.2 - v.2.2| = 1

/-- The burnt set after `t` steps, starting from the fire `B0`, when the set `P s` is protected at step
`s ≥ 1`. At step `t + 1` the firefighters first protect `P (t + 1)`; then the fire spreads to every
neighbour of a burnt vertex that has not been protected at any step `≤ t + 1`. -/
def burnt (B0 : Set V3) (P : ℕ → Finset V3) : ℕ → Set V3
  | 0 => B0
  | t + 1 => burnt B0 P t ∪
      {v : V3 | (∀ s : ℕ, s ≤ t + 1 → v ∉ P s) ∧ ∃ u ∈ burnt B0 P t, Adj3 u v}

/-- Rate `c` contains every finite outbreak: for every finite initial fire there is a schedule with
at most `c * s` (equivalently `⌊c s⌋`) vertices protected at step `s` such that only finitely many
vertices ever burn. -/
def Contains (c : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ B0 : Finset V3, ∃ P : ℕ → Finset V3,
    (∀ s : ℕ, ((P s).card : ℝ) ≤ c * (s : ℝ)) ∧
    (⋃ t : ℕ, burnt (↑B0 : Set V3) P t).Finite

/-- `c* > 32/27`: some rate above `32/27` does not contain every finite outbreak. -/
def Claim : Prop := ∃ c : ℝ, 32 / 27 < c ∧ ¬ Contains c

end OpenProblems.QEDE077
M_fix_reason: M (64/243 ≤ c* ≤ 48/7) contradicts W and the bound field (8/243 ≤ c* ≤ 8, with 8/243 = 2a^2-6a^3 at a=2/9 checked), and M never defines c* or the target; the fix states c*, both versions of the known bounds, and a single open target that improves on either.
prov_reason: Linear order t^{d-2} of firefighters on Z^3 is known; asking for the sharp constant is a new parameter question formulated by QED.

title: Distinct character degrees of the symmetric group
credit: On the irreducible character degrees of symmetric groups and their multiplicities, arXiv:2410.01726 (2024)
premise_risks: arXiv:2410.01726 (preprint, refereeing status unclear): the numerical data for n <= 129 and the suggested limit near 2.5 are context only; Claim does not depend on them.
plain: Conjugate partitions always give representations of S_n of the same dimension, so at most about half of the p(n) irreducible representations can have distinct dimensions. Decide whether the fraction of distinct dimensions tends to a limit, and whether that limit is positive.
math: Let d(n) = #{f^λ : λ ⊢ n} be the number of distinct irreducible character degrees of S_n and p(n) the number of partitions of n. Prove or disprove: d(n)/p(n) converges to a positive limit L as n → ∞.
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-E078: Distinct character degrees of the symmetric group
Conjugate partitions give irreducible representations of S_n of the same dimension, so at most
about half of the p(n) irreducible representations have distinct dimensions. Does the fraction
d(n)/p(n) of distinct dimensions tend to a positive limit?
Informal statement: Let d(n) = #{f^λ : λ ⊢ n} be the number of distinct irreducible character degrees of S_n and p(n) the number of partitions of n. Prove or disprove: d(n)/p(n) converges to a positive limit L as n → ∞.
Formalization notes: The original asks to determine whether lim d(n)/p(n) exists, find it, and
in particular decide whether liminf d(n)/p(n) > 0. Claim is the natural conjecture "the limit
exists and is positive". Proving ¬Claim means: either d(n)/p(n) does not converge, or it
converges to 0. Partitions of n are generated explicitly as weakly decreasing lists of positive
integers summing to n (`partitionsList n`; first part k+1 <= m, remaining parts <= k+1). The
degree f^λ is defined by the hook length formula f^λ = n! / Π_{cells} hook(cell), where the hook
of cell (i,j) is (λ_i - j - 1) + #{k > i : λ_k > j} + 1; the division is exact by the hook length
theorem, so this is the number of standard Young tableaux, i.e. the dimension of the Specht
module. d(n) counts distinct values of this list, p(n) its length (p(n) >= 1). Data: p(40) =
37338, d(40) = 16216 (checked with an independent script implementing these exact definitions);
d(n)/p(n) ∈ [0.40, 0.47] for 20 <= n <= 45; arXiv:2410.01726 suggests p(n)/d(n) may tend to
about 2.5 (a referee suggested π√(2/3)), but this is not part of Claim.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE078

/-- `partitionsAux fuel n m`: all partitions of `n` into parts `<= m`, as weakly decreasing lists.
`fuel` only guarantees termination; `fuel >= n` suffices. -/
def partitionsAux : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → List (List ℕ)
  | 0, n, _ => if n = 0 then [[]] else []
  | fuel + 1, n, m =>
    if n = 0 then [[]] else
      (List.range (min m n)).flatMap (fun k =>
        (partitionsAux fuel (n - (k + 1)) (k + 1)).map (fun l => (k + 1) :: l))

/-- All partitions of `n`, each listed once as a weakly decreasing list of positive parts. -/
def partitionsList (n : ℕ) : List (List ℕ) := partitionsAux n n n

/-- Product of all hook lengths of the Young diagram with row lengths `l`. -/
def hookProduct (l : List ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ∏ i ∈ Finset.range l.length, ∏ j ∈ Finset.range (l.getD i 0),
    ((l.getD i 0 - j - 1) + ((l.drop (i + 1)).filter (fun r => decide (j < r))).length + 1)

/-- Degree of the irreducible character of S_n indexed by `l`, via the hook length formula. -/
def charDegree (n : ℕ) (l : List ℕ) : ℕ := n.factorial / hookProduct l

/-- p(n), the number of partitions of n. -/
def numPartitions (n : ℕ) : ℕ := (partitionsList n).length

/-- d(n), the number of distinct irreducible character degrees of S_n. -/
def numDistinctDegrees (n : ℕ) : ℕ := ((partitionsList n).map (charDegree n)).dedup.length

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∃ L : ℝ, 0 < L ∧
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (numDistinctDegrees n : ℝ) / (numPartitions n : ℝ))
      Filter.atTop (nhds L)

end OpenProblems.QEDE078
M_fix_reason: M is a 'determine whether / find' question. Turned into the single conjecture 'the limit exists and is positive'. The intermediate question liminf > 0 is not separately encoded.
prov_reason: Reviewer notes: already posed in essence in arXiv:2410.01726, which plots p(n)/|cd(S_n)| to n=129, says it is unclear whether a limit exists, and records a referee's guess π√(2/3).

title: Is the Petersen graph common?
premise_risks: arXiv:2610.20149 (2026 preprint): cited background on common graphs; M does not depend on it.
plain: Color the edges of a huge complete graph red and blue. Does a random coloring minimize the number of single-color copies of the Petersen graph?
math: Let $P$ be the Petersen graph ($10$ vertices, $15$ edges) and $m(P)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\min_{\chi}\frac{\#\{\text{monochromatic copies of }P\text{ in }(K_n,\chi)\}}{\#\{\text{copies of }P\text{ in }K_n\}}$, minimum over red/blue colorings $\chi$ of $E(K_n)$. Is $m(P)=2^{-14}$, i.e. is $P$ common? Equivalently, is $t(P,W)+t(P,1-W)\ge 2^{-14}$ for every graphon $W$? If not, determine $m(P)$.
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-E079: Is the Petersen graph common?
Colour the edges of a huge complete graph red and blue. Does a uniformly random colouring
asymptotically minimise the number of monochromatic copies of the Petersen graph?
Informal statement: Let P be the Petersen graph (10 vertices, 15 edges). Is P common, i.e. is
t(P,W) + t(P,1−W) ≥ 2^{−14} for every graphon W? (Equivalently m(P) = 2^{−14}, where m(P) is
the limiting minimum fraction of monochromatic copies of P over red/blue colourings of K_n.)
Formalization notes: Petersen graph on `Fin 10`: outer cycle 0-1-2-3-4-0, spokes i–(i+5),
inner pentagram 5-7-9-6-8-5, given as a list of 15 edges. For a symmetric n × n array A with
entries in [0,1] (a step graphon with n equal parts, diagonal allowed), the homomorphism count
hom(P,A) = ∑_{φ : Fin 10 → Fin n} ∏_{ij ∈ E(P)} A(φ i, φ j) equals n^{10} · t(P, W_A). Since
step graphons are dense in the cut metric and t(P,·) is cut-continuous, "∀ graphons W" is
equivalent to "∀ n, ∀ such A". The complement is the entrywise array 1 − A(i,j) (written as a
function, not Matrix subtraction, to avoid the identity matrix). Proving `Claim` = P is common;
`¬Claim` = an explicit (step) graphon beating the random colouring, i.e. P is uncommon.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE079

/-- The 15 edges of the Petersen graph on `Fin 10`. -/
def petersenEdges : List (Fin 10 × Fin 10) :=
  [(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 4), (4, 0),
   (0, 5), (1, 6), (2, 7), (3, 8), (4, 9),
   (5, 7), (7, 9), (9, 6), (6, 8), (8, 5)]

/-- Homomorphism count of the Petersen graph into the weighted graph `A`. -/
def homP {n : ℕ} (A : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ φ : Fin 10 → Fin n, (petersenEdges.map (fun e => A (φ e.1) (φ e.2))).prod

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (A : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ),
    (∀ i j, A i j = A j i) → (∀ i j, 0 ≤ A i j ∧ A i j ≤ 1) →
    (1 / 2 : ℝ) ^ 14 * (n : ℝ) ^ 10 ≤ homP A + homP (fun i j => 1 - A i j)

end OpenProblems.QEDE079
M_fix_reason: M (already rewritten as the commonness question) is correct; 'if not, determine m(P)' is a fallback and not formalized.
prov_reason: Commonness of specific graphs is a classical programme, but no source found posing or settling the Petersen graph specifically (one search, plus refs).

title: The complex of planar graphs
plain: Planar graphs on n labelled vertices form a simplicial complex, because deleting an edge keeps a graph planar. It is pure, since every maximal planar graph has 3n-6 edges. Its homology turns out not to be that of a wedge of top-dimensional spheres: already for n=6 it is concentrated two degrees lower and has 2-torsion. Determine its homology.
math: Let $\Pi_n$ be the simplicial complex on vertex set $E(K_n)$ whose faces are edge sets of planar graphs; it is pure of dimension $3n-7$. Determine $\tilde H_*(\Pi_n;\mathbb Z)$, or at least $\tilde H_*(\Pi_n;\mathbb Q)$, for all $n$. Known: $\Pi_4$ is a simplex, $\Pi_5=\partial\Delta^9\cong S^8$. For $n=6$ (computed exactly): $\tilde H_*(\Pi_6;\mathbb Q)$ is $\mathbb Q^{15}$ in degree $9=3n-9$ and $0$ elsewhere; $\tilde H_*(\Pi_6;\mathbb F_2)$ is $\mathbb F_2^{15},\mathbb F_2,\mathbb F_2$ in degrees $9,10,11$, so $\tilde H_{10}(\Pi_6;\mathbb Z)$ has $2$-torsion and $\Pi_6$ is not a wedge of spheres. The mod-2 top class is the sum of all triangulations: every face of dimension $3n-8$ of $\Pi_6$ lies in an even number (2 or 4) of facets. Questions: (a) is $\tilde H_*(\Pi_n;\mathbb Q)$ concentrated in degree $3n-9$ for all $n\ge6$, and what is its rank and $S_n$-module structure? (b) Is $\tilde H_{3n-7}(\Pi_n;\mathbb F_2)\ne0$ for all $n\ge5$? Is all torsion 2-torsion?
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-E080: The complex of planar graphs
Planar graphs on n labelled vertices form a simplicial complex Πₙ on the vertex set E(Kₙ) (deleting an edge keeps a graph
planar); it is pure of dimension 3n − 7. For n = 6 its rational reduced homology is ℚ^15 in degree 9 = 3n − 9 and zero
elsewhere, while its mod-2 homology also has classes in degrees 10 and 11, so it is not a wedge of spheres.
Informal statement: Let Πₙ be the simplicial complex on vertex set E(Kₙ) whose faces are edge sets of planar graphs.
Determine H̃_*(Πₙ; ℤ), or at least H̃_*(Πₙ; ℚ). Main question (a): is H̃_*(Πₙ; ℚ) concentrated in degree 3n − 9 for all
n ≥ 6? (Further: its rank and Sₙ-module structure; whether H̃_{3n−7}(Πₙ; 𝔽₂) ≠ 0 for all n ≥ 5; whether all torsion is
2-torsion.)
Formalization notes: Claim formalizes question (a) only (the main yes/no question): for all n ≥ 6 the rational reduced
Betti numbers vanish in every degree other than 3n − 9 ("concentrated" does not assert non-vanishing there).
Edges of Kₙ are pairs (i, j) with i < j in Fin n, linearly ordered by the key i·n + j. Planarity is defined by Wagner's
theorem: no K₅ minor and no K₃,₃ minor, where a minor model is a family of pairwise disjoint vertex sets, each inducing a
connected subgraph, with an edge between the required pairs. `Face n j` = planar edge sets of size j (simplices of
dimension j − 1; the empty face gives the augmentation, so homology is reduced). `bd n j` is the oriented boundary
matrix from size-(j+1) faces to size-j faces, with sign (−1)^(position of the removed edge). The reduced Betti number in
degree j − 1 is `redBetti n j` = dim C_j − rank(∂ out of C_j) − rank(∂ into C_j), computed over ℚ with `Matrix.rank`.
Degree 3n − 9 corresponds to face size 3n − 8. Proving Claim = concentration for all n ≥ 6; ¬Claim = some n ≥ 6 with
nonzero rational homology in another degree.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE080

/-- Edges of `Kₙ`: ordered pairs `(i, j)` with `i < j`. -/
abbrev Edge (n : ℕ) := {p : Fin n × Fin n // p.1 < p.2}

/-- A linear-order key on edges, used for orientation signs. -/
def edgeKey {n : ℕ} (e : Edge n) : ℕ := e.1.1.val * n + e.1.2.val

/-- The simple graph on `Fin n` with edge set `s`. -/
def graphOf {n : ℕ} (s : Finset (Edge n)) : SimpleGraph (Fin n) :=
  SimpleGraph.fromRel (fun u v => ∃ e ∈ s, e.1.1 = u ∧ e.1.2 = v)

/-- `G` has a `K₅` minor. -/
def HasK5Minor {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ B : Fin 5 → Set (Fin n),
    (∀ i, (SimpleGraph.induce (B i) G).Connected) ∧
    (∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (B i) (B j)) ∧
    (∀ i j, i ≠ j → ∃ u ∈ B i, ∃ v ∈ B j, G.Adj u v)

/-- `G` has a `K₃,₃` minor (branch sets `0,1,2` on one side, `3,4,5` on the other). -/
def HasK33Minor {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ B : Fin 6 → Set (Fin n),
    (∀ i, (SimpleGraph.induce (B i) G).Connected) ∧
    (∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (B i) (B j)) ∧
    (∀ i j : Fin 6, i.val < 3 → 3 ≤ j.val → ∃ u ∈ B i, ∃ v ∈ B j, G.Adj u v)

/-- Planarity, via Wagner's theorem. -/
def IsPlanar {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) : Prop := ¬ HasK5Minor G ∧ ¬ HasK33Minor G

/-- Faces of `Πₙ` with `j` elements (simplices of dimension `j - 1`). -/
abbrev Face (n j : ℕ) := {s : Finset (Edge n) // s.card = j ∧ IsPlanar (graphOf s)}

noncomputable instance instFintypeFace (n j : ℕ) : Fintype (Face n j) := Fintype.ofFinite _

/-- Oriented boundary matrix from faces of size `j + 1` (columns) to faces of size `j` (rows). -/
noncomputable def bd (n j : ℕ) : Matrix (Face n j) (Face n (j + 1)) ℚ :=
  fun τ σ =>
    if τ.1 ⊆ σ.1 then
      (-1 : ℚ) ^ (σ.1.filter (fun f => ∀ e ∈ σ.1 \ τ.1, edgeKey f < edgeKey e)).card
    else 0

/-- Rational reduced Betti number of `Πₙ` in degree `j - 1` (faces of size `j`). -/
noncomputable def redBetti (n : ℕ) : ℕ → ℕ
  | 0 => Fintype.card (Face n 0) - (bd n 0).rank
  | (j + 1) => Fintype.card (Face n (j + 1)) - (bd n j).rank - (bd n (j + 1)).rank

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, 6 ≤ n → ∀ j : ℕ, j ≠ 3 * n - 8 → redBetti n j = 0

end OpenProblems.QEDE080
prov_reason: No literature on the simplicial complex of planar graphs was found (planarity is absent from Jonsson's survey of monotone graph properties); the question and the n = 6 data are QED's.

title: A super-constant-degree SoS integrality gap for Unique Games
credit: Barak, Sum-of-Squares open problems (lecture notes); Barak & Steurer 2014, arXiv:1404.5236
plain: Construct Unique Games instances with value <= eps on which degree-d Sum-of-Squares has value >= 1-eps, for some d = omega(1) (any slowly growing function of n), or show degree-O(1) SoS achieves a (1-eps, delta) distinguishing guarantee on all UG instances.
math: (Gap) For every eps>0 there is q=q(eps) such that for every degree D there is a Unique Games instance over [q] with optimum <= eps whose degree-2D SoS (Lasserre) value is >= 1-eps. Claim := Gap; ¬Claim is exactly the algorithmic alternative.
refs: Barak, Brandão, Harrow, Kelner, Steurer, Zhou, Hypercontractivity, sum-of-squares proofs, and their applications, STOC 2012, arXiv:1205.4484
Khot, Minzer, Safra, Pseudorandom sets in Grassmann graph have near-perfect expansion, FOCS 2018
Barak, Sum of Squares: open problems (lecture notes)
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-E081: A super-constant-degree SoS integrality gap for Unique Games
Construct Unique Games instances of optimum value at most ε on which the degree-d Sum-of-Squares
relaxation still has value at least 1 - ε, with alphabet size depending only on ε and degree d
growing without bound; the alternative is that constant-degree SoS distinguishes (1-ε)-satisfiable
from δ-satisfiable instances for every alphabet size.
Informal statement: (Gap) For every ε > 0 there is q = q(ε) such that for every degree bound D there is
a Unique Games instance over alphabet [q] with optimum ≤ ε on which the degree-2D SoS (Lasserre)
relaxation has value ≥ 1 - ε (equivalently: a family of instances of growing size n with
degree d(n) = ω(1) gaps). The (Algorithm) alternative in the original statement is exactly the
negation of (Gap), so the original disjunction was a tautology; Claim is (Gap) alone.
Formalization notes: A `UGInstance q` has `n` variables, `m` constraints, the e-th constraint asks
`perm e (f (src e)) = f (dst e)`. `value f` is the satisfied fraction. The SoS relaxation of degree 2D
uses Boolean variables `X (v,i)` ("v gets label i") and a pseudo-expectation: an ℝ-linear functional
`L` on `MvPolynomial (Fin n × Fin q) ℝ` with `L 1 = 1`, `L (p*p) ≥ 0` for `deg p ≤ D`, and
`L (p * g) = 0` for each constraint polynomial `g` (`X^2 - X`, `∑_i X (v,i) - 1`) whenever
`deg p + deg g ≤ 2D`. The SoS value is the sup of `L objective`; "value ≥ 1 - ε" is encoded by
existence of such an `L` (the sup is attained by compactness, so this is equivalent).
Proving `Claim` = constructing the super-constant-degree gap (strong evidence for UGC-type hardness of SoS).
Proving `¬Claim` = there are ε, δ (take δ = ε) such that for every q some constant degree D refutes
all instances of value ≤ ε, i.e. the algorithmic side (which would refute UGC unless P = NP).
Note: for fixed instance size, degree ≥ n·q SoS is exact, so the instances must grow with D.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE081

/-- A Unique Games instance over alphabet `Fin q`: `n` variables, `m` permutation constraints. -/
structure UGInstance (q : ℕ) where
  n : ℕ
  m : ℕ
  src : Fin m → Fin n
  dst : Fin m → Fin n
  perm : Fin m → Equiv.Perm (Fin q)

/-- Fraction of constraints satisfied by the labelling `f`. -/
noncomputable def UGInstance.value {q : ℕ} (I : UGInstance q) (f : Fin I.n → Fin q) : ℝ :=
  ((Finset.univ.filter (fun e : Fin I.m => I.perm e (f (I.src e)) = f (I.dst e))).card : ℝ) /
    (I.m : ℝ)

/-- The degree-2 objective polynomial: average over constraints of `∑_i x_{src,i} x_{dst,π i}`. -/
noncomputable def UGInstance.objective {q : ℕ} (I : UGInstance q) :
    MvPolynomial (Fin I.n × Fin q) ℝ :=
  MvPolynomial.C ((I.m : ℝ)⁻¹) *
    ∑ e : Fin I.m, ∑ i : Fin q,
      MvPolynomial.X (I.src e, i) * MvPolynomial.X (I.dst e, I.perm e i)

/-- `L` is a degree-`2D` SoS pseudo-expectation for the Boolean one-hot encoding of `I`. -/
def IsPseudoExpectation {q : ℕ} (I : UGInstance q) (D : ℕ)
    (L : MvPolynomial (Fin I.n × Fin q) ℝ →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) : Prop :=
  L 1 = 1 ∧
  (∀ p : MvPolynomial (Fin I.n × Fin q) ℝ, p.totalDegree ≤ D → 0 ≤ L (p * p)) ∧
  (∀ (p : MvPolynomial (Fin I.n × Fin q) ℝ) (v : Fin I.n) (i : Fin q),
      p.totalDegree + 2 ≤ 2 * D →
      L (p * (MvPolynomial.X (v, i) * MvPolynomial.X (v, i) - MvPolynomial.X (v, i))) = 0) ∧
  (∀ (p : MvPolynomial (Fin I.n × Fin q) ℝ) (v : Fin I.n),
      p.totalDegree + 1 ≤ 2 * D →
      L (p * ((∑ i : Fin q, MvPolynomial.X (v, i)) - 1)) = 0)

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ q : ℕ, ∀ D : ℕ, ∃ I : UGInstance q,
    0 < I.m ∧
    (∀ f : Fin I.n → Fin q, I.value f ≤ ε) ∧
    ∃ L : MvPolynomial (Fin I.n × Fin q) ℝ →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ,
      IsPseudoExpectation I D L ∧ 1 - ε ≤ L I.objective

end OpenProblems.QEDE081
M_fix_reason: As written, M is the disjunction of (Gap) and (Algorithm), and (Algorithm) is exactly the negation of (Gap) (take delta = eps, use monotonicity in degree). So the disjunction is a tautology, and any solver could prove it by excluded middle.

review_note: Context (Nov 2026): OpenAI's preprint "The Unique Games Theorem" proves UGC; together with P ≠ NP this would imply the Claim, but P ≠ NP is not known, so the Claim remains open. Context (AI-lab announcement, treated as correct): OpenAI 102: The Unique Games Conjecture and optimal approximation thresholds (The Unique Games Theorem). UGC is now a theorem (3SAT reduces to UG with completeness 1-eps, soundness delta, fixed alphabet). If not-Claim held, constant-degree SoS would decide those instances in poly time, giving P=NP. title: Binary-error LWE with linearly many samples
credit: Micciancio, Peikert, Hardness of SIS and LWE with small parameters, CRYPTO 2013; Arora, Ge, ICALP 2011.
plain: For LWE with secret in Z_q^n (q = poly(n)) and errors uniform in {0,1}, given m = C*n samples for a fixed constant C > 1, either give a polynomial-time (or 2^{o(n)}) algorithm, or prove hardness from standard LWE/worst-case lattice problems for m = C*n (beyond the n(1+O(1/log n)) samples of Micciancio-Peikert).
math: Fix q = q(n) with 2 <= q(n) <= poly(n) and a constant C > 1; m = ceil(Cn). Decision binary-error LWE: given (A, b), A uniform in Z_q^{m x n}, b = As + e mod q (s uniform, e uniform in {0,1}^m) or b uniform. Show that for every such C and q either (a) some randomized 2^{o(n)}-time algorithm distinguishes with non-negligible advantage, or (b) the problem is hard for polynomial time (no non-negligible advantage) assuming standard decision LWE is hard for some standard parameter family (dimension polynomially related to n, poly(n) modulus and samples, discrete Gaussian error of width alpha q' >= 2 sqrt(n')). Known: Arora-Ge solves m ~ n^2 in poly time; Micciancio-Peikert give (b) for m = n(1+O(1/log n)).

Arora, Ge, New algorithms for learning in presence of errors, ICALP 2011
Albrecht, Cid, Faugère, Fitzpatrick, Perret, Algebraic algorithms for LWE problems, ACM CCA 2015
