import Mathlib
/-! QED-E087: From density to Kolmogorov typicality of positive entropy in symplectic families
Berger and Turaev showed that families of area-preserving surface maps having positive metric entropy at every
parameter are dense among smooth families. Show this is typical, i.e. holds for a Kolmogorov-generic set of families,
or find a robust obstruction.
Informal statement (sharpened): Take `Σ = 𝕋² = ℝ²/ℤ²` with the standard area form. For `k ≥ 1` let `𝓕_k` be the
space of `C^∞` families `(f_p)_{p ∈ [0,1]^k}` of area- and orientation-preserving (= symplectic) diffeomorphisms of
`𝕋²` such that every `f_p` has an elliptic periodic point, with the `C^∞` topology on `(p, x) ↦ f_p(x)`. Let
`𝓕_+ = {families with h_Leb(f_p) > 0 for Lebesgue-a.e. p}`. Claim: for every `k ≥ 1`, `𝓕_+` is Kolmogorov typical,
i.e. contains a countable intersection of open subsets that are dense in `𝓕_k`. ¬Claim: for some `k ≥ 1`, `𝓕_+`
contains no residual subset of `𝓕_k` (a robust obstruction).
Formalization notes:
* Surface: `𝕋²`, represented by lifts `f : ℝ² → ℝ²` with `f(x + m) = f(x) + A m` (`m ∈ ℤ²`, `A ∈ SL₂(ℤ)`),
  `f` bijective and `C^∞`, `det Df ≡ 1`. Such `f` descends to a symplectic `C^∞` diffeomorphism of `𝕋²` and every one
  lifts. A lift is determined up to an integer translation; the lifted family space covers the space of torus
  families by a local homeomorphism and all sets used are saturated, so open/dense/residual notions agree.
  A fixed concrete surface is a sharpening of "fix a compact surface Σ".
* Families: `F : ℝ^k × ℝ² → ℝ²`, `C^∞` jointly, with `F(p, ·)` such a lift for each `p ∈ [0,1]^k` (values outside
  the cube are irrelevant). `C^∞` (Whitney/Fréchet) topology on the compact set `[0,1]^k × 𝕋²`: basic
  neighbourhoods `{G : ‖D^j(G − F)(z)‖ < ε for all j ≤ r, z ∈ [0,1]^k × [0,1]²}` (derivatives of `G − F` are
  `ℤ²`-periodic in `x` for `A_G = A_F`, and `A` is locally constant, so `[0,1]²` suffices). This is the topology of
  `C^∞([0,1]^k × 𝕋², 𝕋²)` used by Berger–Turaev.
* Elliptic periodic point: `f^N(x) ≡ x mod ℤ²`, `N ≥ 1`, `|tr D(f^N)(x)| < 2` (with `det = 1` this means the
  eigenvalues are non-real on the unit circle). Berger–Turaev's space `Symp^∞_el` additionally asks the elliptic
  point to be non-degenerate (twist, no strong resonance); we use plain ellipticity, as in the problem's `F`.
  (Non-degeneracy is an open dense condition at each elliptic point; we expect, but do not claim, that the
  Berger–Turaev subspace is open and dense in `𝓕_k`, in which case the two notions of typicality coincide.)
* Metric entropy: by Pesin's formula (Ruelle inequality + Pesin equality for `C²` area-preserving surface
  diffeomorphisms), `h_Leb(f) = ∫ λ⁺ dLeb` with `λ⁺(x) = lim (1/n) log ‖Df^n(x)‖ ≥ 0`, existing a.e. (Oseledets).
  Hence `h_Leb(f) > 0` iff `{x : liminf (1/n) log ‖Df^n(x)‖ > 0}` has positive area, which is how `PosEntropy` is
  written (Berger–Turaev use the same integrand `liminf (1/n) log ‖Df^n‖`). Norms: sup norm on `ℝ × ℝ`; any norm
  gives the same exponent.
* Kolmogorov typicality (Berger–Turaev): containing a countable intersection of open dense subsets of the family
  space; with `k` arbitrary. `Claim` asks it for every `k ≥ 1`.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE087
noncomputable section
open MeasureTheory Filter

/-- The plane `ℝ²`. -/
abbrev Pt := ℝ × ℝ
/-- Parameter space `ℝ^k`. -/
abbrev Par (k : ℕ) := Fin k → ℝ

/-- `m ∈ ℤ²` as a point of `ℝ²`. -/
def lat (m : ℤ × ℤ) : Pt := ((m.1 : ℝ), (m.2 : ℝ))

/-- Entries of the Jacobian matrix. -/
def j11 (f : Pt → Pt) (x : Pt) : ℝ := (fderiv ℝ f x ((1 : ℝ), (0 : ℝ))).1
def j12 (f : Pt → Pt) (x : Pt) : ℝ := (fderiv ℝ f x ((0 : ℝ), (1 : ℝ))).1
def j21 (f : Pt → Pt) (x : Pt) : ℝ := (fderiv ℝ f x ((1 : ℝ), (0 : ℝ))).2
def j22 (f : Pt → Pt) (x : Pt) : ℝ := (fderiv ℝ f x ((0 : ℝ), (1 : ℝ))).2

/-- Jacobian determinant. -/
def jdet (f : Pt → Pt) (x : Pt) : ℝ := j11 f x * j22 f x - j12 f x * j21 f x
/-- Jacobian trace. -/
def jtr (f : Pt → Pt) (x : Pt) : ℝ := j11 f x + j22 f x

/-- `f` is the lift of a symplectic `C^∞` diffeomorphism of `𝕋² = ℝ²/ℤ²`. -/
def IsTorusSymp (f : Pt → Pt) : Prop :=
  (∀ r : ℕ, ContDiff ℝ r f) ∧ Function.Bijective f ∧
  (∃ a b c e : ℤ, a * e - b * c = 1 ∧ ∀ x : Pt, ∀ m : ℤ × ℤ,
      f (x + lat m) = f x + lat (a * m.1 + b * m.2, c * m.1 + e * m.2)) ∧
  ∀ x : Pt, jdet f x = 1

/-- `f` has an elliptic periodic point on `𝕋²`. -/
def HasEllipticPeriodicPoint (f : Pt → Pt) : Prop :=
  ∃ x : Pt, ∃ N : ℕ, 0 < N ∧ (∃ m : ℤ × ℤ, f^[N] x = x + lat m) ∧ |jtr (f^[N]) x| < 2

/-- The fundamental domain `[0,1]²`. -/
def unitSq : Set Pt := Set.Icc ((0 : ℝ), (0 : ℝ)) ((1 : ℝ), (1 : ℝ))

/-- Positive metric entropy w.r.t. area: positive Lyapunov exponent on a set of positive area. -/
def PosEntropy (f : Pt → Pt) : Prop :=
  0 < volume {x ∈ unitSq | ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ε * (n : ℝ) ≤ Real.log ‖fderiv ℝ (f^[n]) x‖}

/-- The parameter cube `[0,1]^k`. -/
def cube (k : ℕ) : Set (Par k) := {p : Par k | ∀ i : Fin k, p i ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1}

/-- Smooth `k`-parameter families of symplectic torus diffeomorphisms. -/
def Fam (k : ℕ) : Set (Par k × Pt → Pt) :=
  {F | (∀ r : ℕ, ContDiff ℝ r F) ∧ ∀ p ∈ cube k, IsTorusSymp (fun x : Pt => F (p, x))}

/-- Families each of whose members has an elliptic periodic point (the space `𝓕_k`). -/
def Ell (k : ℕ) : Set (Par k × Pt → Pt) :=
  {F | F ∈ Fam k ∧ ∀ p ∈ cube k, HasEllipticPeriodicPoint (fun x : Pt => F (p, x))}

/-- `𝓕_+`: positive metric entropy for Lebesgue-a.e. parameter. -/
def Plus (k : ℕ) : Set (Par k × Pt → Pt) :=
  {F | ∀ᵐ p ∂(volume.restrict (cube k)), PosEntropy (fun x : Pt => F (p, x))}

/-- `G` is in the basic `C^r`, `ε`-neighbourhood of `F`. -/
def Near (k r : ℕ) (ε : ℝ) (F G : Par k × Pt → Pt) : Prop :=
  ∀ j : ℕ, j ≤ r → ∀ z ∈ cube k ×ˢ unitSq,
    ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ j (fun w : Par k × Pt => G w - F w) z‖ < ε

/-- Open subset of the family space (`C^∞` topology). -/
def IsOpenFam (k : ℕ) (U : Set (Par k × Pt → Pt)) : Prop :=
  U ⊆ Fam k ∧ ∀ F ∈ U, ∃ r : ℕ, ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ∀ G ∈ Fam k, Near k r ε F G → G ∈ U

/-- `D ∩ Y` is dense in `Y`. -/
def DenseIn (k : ℕ) (D Y : Set (Par k × Pt → Pt)) : Prop :=
  ∀ F ∈ Y, ∀ r : ℕ, ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ G ∈ D ∩ Y, Near k r ε F G

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ k : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → ∃ D : ℕ → Set (Par k × Pt → Pt),
    (∀ i : ℕ, IsOpenFam k (D i) ∧ DenseIn k (D i) (Ell k)) ∧ Ell k ∩ (⋂ i, D i) ⊆ Plus k

end
end OpenProblems.QEDE087
M_fix_reason: M is ambiguous: 'having an elliptic periodic point' does not say at which parameters; 'Kolmogorov-typical (in their sense)' imports an undefined notion; and the 'or exhibit an open set' alternative is not the negation of the first, so the problem is not a single yes/no claim. The fix states the requirement at every parameter, makes typicality explicit (to be checked against Berger-Turaev's definition), and phrases the obstruction as the negation.
prov_reason: Upgrades Berger-Turaev's density theorem (Thm B) for positive metric entropy in symplectic families to typicality; the notes call it the conspicuous gap in their typicality results rather than a question they pose explicitly.

title: Integrability of the egg-crate torus
credit: V. V. Kozlov, non-integrability of perturbed geodesic flows on the torus (Poincaré-Kozlov theory; 'Symmetries, Topology and Resonances in Hamiltonian Mechanics', 1996); Paternain, Taimanov for entropy obstructions
plain: Put the surface z = ε sin x sin y over a flat square torus. Show its geodesic flow is never integrable, however small the bumps are.
math: For $\varepsilon>0$ let $g_\varepsilon$ be the metric on $\mathbb T^2=\mathbb R^2/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^2$ induced from the graph $z=\varepsilon\sin x\sin y$, i.e. $g_\varepsilon=dx^2+dy^2+\varepsilon^2(\cos x\sin y\,dx+\sin x\cos y\,dy)^2$. Prove that for every $\varepsilon>0$ the geodesic flow on $T^*\mathbb T^2\setminus0$ has no real-analytic first integral functionally independent of the Hamiltonian (for example, by showing positive topological entropy).
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-E088: Integrability of the egg-crate torus
Put the surface z = ε sin x sin y over the flat square torus ℝ²/(2πℤ)². Show that its geodesic
flow is never integrable (no extra real-analytic first integral), however small ε > 0 is.
Informal statement: For ε > 0 let g_ε be the metric on 𝕋² = ℝ²/(2πℤ)² induced from the graph
z = ε sin x sin y, i.e. g_ε = dx² + dy² + ε²(cos x sin y dx + sin x cos y dy)². Prove that for
every ε > 0 the geodesic flow on T*𝕋² \ 0 has no real-analytic first integral functionally
independent of the Hamiltonian.
Formalization notes: Phase-space points are `q : Fin 4 → ℝ` with q 0 = x, q 1 = y, q 2 = p_x,
q 3 = p_y. With w = (cos x sin y, sin x cos y), g_ε = I + ε² w wᵀ, so
g_ε⁻¹ = I − ε² w wᵀ / (1 + ε²|w|²) and the geodesic Hamiltonian is
H_ε = ½ (p_x² + p_y² − ε² (w·p)² / (1 + ε²|w|²)) (`ham`). T*𝕋² \ 0 is modelled by the open set
`U = {p ≠ 0}` in ℝ⁴ together with 2π-periodicity of F in x and y. `pd F i q` is the partial
derivative ∂F/∂q_i (Fréchet derivative applied to the i-th basis vector) and `poisson` is the
canonical Poisson bracket Σ (∂F/∂x_k ∂G/∂p_k − ∂F/∂p_k ∂G/∂x_k). An additional first integral is
an F that is real-analytic on U (`AnalyticOnNhd`), 2π-periodic in x and y, Poisson-commutes with
H_ε on U, and is functionally independent of H_ε, i.e. dF ∧ dH_ε ≠ 0 at some point of U (for
real-analytic F on the connected set U this is equivalent to independence on an open dense set).
Proving `Claim` means: for every ε > 0 no such F exists (non-integrability; positive topological
entropy would suffice by Paternain/Taimanov). Proving `¬Claim` means exhibiting some ε > 0 and
such an integral. Kozlov's theorem already excludes integrals analytic in ε.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE088

/-- The geodesic Hamiltonian of the egg-crate metric `g_ε` in coordinates `(x, y, p_x, p_y)`. -/
noncomputable def ham (ε : ℝ) (q : Fin 4 → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  let w1 : ℝ := Real.cos (q 0) * Real.sin (q 1)
  let w2 : ℝ := Real.sin (q 0) * Real.cos (q 1)
  (1 / 2 : ℝ) * (q 2 ^ 2 + q 3 ^ 2
    - ε ^ 2 * (w1 * q 2 + w2 * q 3) ^ 2 / (1 + ε ^ 2 * (w1 ^ 2 + w2 ^ 2)))

/-- Partial derivative of `F` in the `i`-th coordinate at `q`. -/
noncomputable def pd (F : (Fin 4 → ℝ) → ℝ) (i : Fin 4) (q : Fin 4 → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  fderiv ℝ F q (Pi.single i (1 : ℝ))

/-- Canonical Poisson bracket `{F, G}` with positions `q 0, q 1` and momenta `q 2, q 3`. -/
noncomputable def poisson (F G : (Fin 4 → ℝ) → ℝ) (q : Fin 4 → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  pd F 0 q * pd G 2 q + pd F 1 q * pd G 3 q - pd F 2 q * pd G 0 q - pd F 3 q * pd G 1 q

/-- The cotangent bundle minus the zero section (before quotienting by periods): `p ≠ 0`. -/
def U : Set (Fin 4 → ℝ) := {q | q 2 ≠ 0 ∨ q 3 ≠ 0}

/-- `F` is 2π-periodic in both position coordinates, i.e. a function on `T*𝕋²`. -/
def IsTorusPeriodic (F : (Fin 4 → ℝ) → ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ q : Fin 4 → ℝ, F (Function.update q 0 (q 0 + 2 * Real.pi)) = F q) ∧
  (∀ q : Fin 4 → ℝ, F (Function.update q 1 (q 1 + 2 * Real.pi)) = F q)

/-- `F` is a real-analytic first integral of the geodesic flow of `g_ε`, independent of `H_ε`. -/
def IsExtraIntegral (ε : ℝ) (F : (Fin 4 → ℝ) → ℝ) : Prop :=
  AnalyticOnNhd ℝ F U ∧ IsTorusPeriodic F ∧
  (∀ q ∈ U, poisson F (ham ε) q = 0) ∧
  ∃ q ∈ U, ∃ i j : Fin 4, pd F i q * pd (ham ε) j q - pd F j q * pd (ham ε) i q ≠ 0

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ¬ ∃ F : (Fin 4 → ℝ) → ℝ, IsExtraIntegral ε F

end OpenProblems.QEDE088
prov_reason: Kozlov's theorem rules out integrals analytic in the parameter ε for such trigonometric perturbations; the fixed-ε, all-ε>0 non-integrability for this explicit egg-crate surface is a new strengthening not posed in the refs.

title: Positive metric entropy for the x^4+y^4 billiard
credit: O. Knill et al., billiards in l^p unit balls (lpbilliards.pdf, Harvard); positive metric entropy for smooth convex billiards / standard-map-type problem (classical open problem)
plain: The billiard table x^4 + y^4 <= 1 is smooth and convex, but its curvature vanishes at four points, so (by Mather) it has no caustics. Its phase space mixes stable islands with apparently chaotic regions. Prove that the chaos is real: on a set of positive measure, nearby trajectories separate exponentially fast.
math:
Let $\Phi$ be the billiard map of $\Omega=\{x^4+y^4\le1\}$, preserving the Liouville measure $
u=\sin	heta\,ds\,d	heta$. Prove that $h_
u(\Phi)>0$; equivalently, by Pesin's formula, that $\Phi$ has a nonzero Lyapunov exponent on a set of positive $
u$-measure.
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-E089: Positive metric entropy for the x^4+y^4 billiard
The billiard table x⁴ + y⁴ ≤ 1 is smooth and convex, but its curvature vanishes at four points, so
(by Mather) it has no caustics. Its phase space mixes stable islands with apparently chaotic
regions. Prove that the chaos is real: on a set of positive measure, nearby trajectories separate
exponentially fast.
Informal statement: Let Φ be the billiard map of Ω = {x⁴ + y⁴ ≤ 1}, preserving the Liouville
measure ν = sin θ ds dθ. Prove that h_ν(Φ) > 0; equivalently, by Pesin's formula, that Φ has a
nonzero Lyapunov exponent on a set of positive ν-measure. (Formalized in the Lyapunov form.)
Formalization notes:
* Phase space. We realise the billiard map in ambient coordinates: a state is (q, v) ∈ ℝ² × ℝ²,
  q the collision point on ∂Ω = {x⁴ + y⁴ = 1}, v the outgoing unit velocity (pointing into Ω).
  The phase space is M = {(q,v) : q ∈ ∂Ω, |v| = 1, v inward}, an open annulus.
* The map. `nextTime q v = sup {t ≥ 0 : q + t v ∈ Ω}` is the free flight time to the next
  collision (Ω is compact and strictly convex, so for (q,v) ∈ M this is the second intersection
  of the chord with ∂Ω). The new velocity is the specular reflection of v in the tangent line at
  the new point q' (normal ∇(x⁴+y⁴)(q') ∥ (q'₁³, q'₂³) ≠ 0). `billiard` is defined by these
  formulas on all of (ℝ²)²; it maps M to M and agrees on M with the Birkhoff billiard map Φ.
  Near M it is real-analytic: the exit time is the larger root of t ↦ F(q + t v) = 1, a simple
  root since a chord of a strictly convex curve is transversal at its endpoints (implicit
  function theorem), so values off M only serve to make `fderiv` meaningful; they never enter
  the tangent cocycle (below).
* Chart. `chart (φ, θ)` = (q(φ), cos θ·T(φ) + sin θ·N(φ)), where q(φ) = r(φ)(cos φ, sin φ),
  r(φ) = (cos⁴φ + sin⁴φ)^(-1/4) is the polar parametrisation of ∂Ω (analytic since
  cos⁴ + sin⁴ ≥ 1/2), T the positively oriented unit tangent and N = inward unit normal; θ is
  the Birkhoff angle between v and the tangent. On (0,2π) × (0,π) this is an analytic
  diffeomorphism onto M minus a null curve, so Lebesgue measure dφ dθ and ν = sin θ ds dθ
  (ds = |q'(φ)| dφ) are mutually absolutely continuous there: "positive ν-measure" = "positive
  dφ dθ-measure".
* Lyapunov exponent. `jac n p = D(Φⁿ ∘ chart)(p)`; by the chain rule this is
  DΦⁿ|_{T M} ∘ D chart(p), which only involves Φ on M (Φⁿ ∘ chart maps into M). D chart(p) is
  injective, so ‖jac n p‖ is comparable, up to constants depending only on p, to the norm of the
  tangent cocycle DΦⁿ(x) : T_x M → T_{Φⁿx} M for the metric induced from ℝ⁴. This metric is
  uniformly equivalent to the (s, θ) chart metric, and passing to the Birkhoff coordinates
  (s, cos θ) changes the cocycle by factors bounded by C/sin θ(Φⁿx); since log(1/sin θ) is
  ν-integrable, Birkhoff's ergodic theorem gives (1/n) log(1/sin θ(Φⁿx)) → 0 ν-a.e. So the
  upper exponent limsup (1/n) log ‖jac n p‖ is the standard top Lyapunov exponent λ⁺ a.e.
  "λ⁺(p) > 0" is encoded as: ∃ λ > 0 with ‖jac n p‖ ≥ e^{λn} for infinitely many n.
* Since Φ preserves the smooth measure ν, exponents come in pairs ±λ, and by Pesin's entropy
  formula (Katok–Strelcyn version for billiards / smooth maps with tempered singularities) plus
  Ruelle's inequality, h_ν(Φ) = ∫ λ⁺ dν; so h_ν(Φ) > 0 ⇔ λ⁺ > 0 on a set of positive measure.
  `fderiv` junk (value 0 where not differentiable) can only shrink the set, so it cannot make
  `Claim` cheaply true; and Φ is differentiable at all chart points, so it does not bias ¬Claim.
* Proving `Claim` = positive metric entropy (nonzero Lyapunov exponent on positive measure).
  Proving `¬Claim` = Lyapunov exponents vanish ν-a.e. (zero metric entropy).
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE089
noncomputable section

/-- The quartic `F(x,y) = x⁴ + y⁴`; the table is `Ω = {F ≤ 1}`. -/
def quartic (q : ℝ × ℝ) : ℝ := q.1 ^ 4 + q.2 ^ 4

/-- Free flight time from `q` in direction `v` until leaving `Ω`. -/
def nextTime (q v : ℝ × ℝ) : ℝ := sSup {t : ℝ | 0 ≤ t ∧ quartic (q + t • v) ≤ 1}

/-- Specular reflection of `v` in the tangent line of `∂Ω` at `q` (normal `∥ (q₁³, q₂³)`). -/
def reflect (q v : ℝ × ℝ) : ℝ × ℝ :=
  v - (2 * (v.1 * q.1 ^ 3 + v.2 * q.2 ^ 3) / (q.1 ^ 6 + q.2 ^ 6)) • ((q.1 ^ 3, q.2 ^ 3) : ℝ × ℝ)

/-- The billiard map on states `(collision point, outgoing velocity)`. -/
def billiard (z : (ℝ × ℝ) × (ℝ × ℝ)) : (ℝ × ℝ) × (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  let q' : ℝ × ℝ := z.1 + nextTime z.1 z.2 • z.2
  (q', reflect q' z.2)

/-- Polar radius of `∂Ω`: `r(φ) = (cos⁴ φ + sin⁴ φ)^(-1/4)`. -/
def radius (φ : ℝ) : ℝ := (Real.cos φ ^ 4 + Real.sin φ ^ 4) ^ (-(1 / 4 : ℝ))

/-- Boundary point with polar angle `φ`. -/
def bdry (φ : ℝ) : ℝ × ℝ := (radius φ * Real.cos φ, radius φ * Real.sin φ)

/-- Chart `(φ, θ) ↦ (q(φ), cos θ · T + sin θ · N)` of the phase space, with `T` the positively
oriented unit tangent and `N` the inward unit normal at `q(φ)`. -/
def chart (p : ℝ × ℝ) : (ℝ × ℝ) × (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  let q : ℝ × ℝ := bdry p.1
  let g : ℝ := Real.sqrt (q.1 ^ 6 + q.2 ^ 6)
  let T : ℝ × ℝ := (-(q.2 ^ 3) / g, q.1 ^ 3 / g)
  let N : ℝ × ℝ := (-(q.1 ^ 3) / g, -(q.2 ^ 3) / g)
  (q, Real.cos p.2 • T + Real.sin p.2 • N)

/-- Derivative of `Φⁿ ∘ chart` at `p` (the tangent cocycle read in the chart). -/
def jac (n : ℕ) (p : ℝ × ℝ) : (ℝ × ℝ) →L[ℝ] ((ℝ × ℝ) × (ℝ × ℝ)) :=
  fderiv ℝ (fun x : ℝ × ℝ => (billiard^[n]) (chart x)) p

/-- Positive top Lyapunov exponent on a set of positive Liouville measure. -/
def Claim : Prop :=
  0 < MeasureTheory.volume
    {p : ℝ × ℝ | p ∈ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) (2 * Real.pi) ×ˢ Set.Ioo (0 : ℝ) Real.pi ∧
      ∃ lam : ℝ, 0 < lam ∧
        ∃ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop, Real.exp (lam * (n : ℝ)) ≤ ‖jac n p‖}

end
end OpenProblems.QEDE089
prov_reason: Knill and coauthors studied exactly the l^p-ball billiards, proved positive topological entropy and found elliptic orbits, and left positive metric entropy open (numerics only, about 0.65 near p=4); the reviewer notes this is not novel.

title: Three identical vortices on a square torus are chaotic
credit: Borisov, Mamaev, Kilin, Regul. Chaotic Dyn. (2019); survey arXiv:2003.00716 (Thm 7); Stremler-Aref (1999, chao-dyn/9907038) for the zero-circulation integrable case
plain: On a flat torus, three point vortices with total circulation zero form an integrable system (Stremler-Aref), but for vortices of equal strength even three are believed chaotic, from numerics only. Prove that three identical point vortices on the square torus are not integrable; the same question is open for four.
math: For N = 3 the reduced flow on M_3 has no real-analytic first integral functionally independent of H (Claim); the N = 4 analogue is a separate proposition ClaimN4, not part of Claim.
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-E090: Three identical vortices on a square torus are chaotic
On a flat torus, three point vortices with total circulation zero form an integrable system
(Stremler–Aref), but for vortices of equal strength even three are believed chaotic, from numerics
only. Prove that three identical point vortices on the square torus are not integrable; the same
question is open for four.
Informal statement: Let G be the Green function of 𝕋 = ℂ/(ℤ + iℤ) (ΔG = δ₀ − 1) and
H = −Σ_{i<j} G(z_i − z_j) on {(z_1,…,z_N) ∈ 𝕋^N : z_i ≠ z_j} with symplectic form Σ dx_i ∧ dy_i.
The centre Z = Σ z_i ∈ 𝕋 is conserved; the reduced space M_N = {Z = Z_0}/((1/N)ℤ[i]/ℤ[i]) is
symplectic of dimension 2N − 2. Prove that for N = 3 the reduced flow on M_3 has no real-analytic
first integral functionally independent of H. (`Claim` is the N = 3 statement; the N = 4 analogue
is the separate proposition `ClaimN4`.)
Formalization notes:
* Green function. Instead of a theta-function formula we characterise G: `IsTorusGreen G` says
  G : ℂ → ℝ is ℤ[i]-periodic, real-analytic off the lattice, has Laplacian −1 off the lattice, and
  G(z) − (1/2π) log|z| is bounded on a punctured disc at 0. This is exactly ΔG = δ₀ − 1 on 𝕋
  (the log term carries the unit point mass), and it determines G up to an additive constant:
  the difference of two such functions is periodic, harmonic off the lattice and bounded near it,
  hence (removable singularities) a bounded entire harmonic function, i.e. a constant. Constants
  do not change H's flow or its integrals, so `∀ G, IsTorusGreen G → …` is the statement for
  the true G. To rule out vacuity, `Claim` also asserts `∃ G, IsTorusGreen G` (true: G(z) =
  (1/2π) log|θ₁(πz | i)| − (Im z)²/2, a standard fact, not the open part).
* Lifted model of M_N. Configurations are z ∈ ℂ^N (`Fin N → ℂ`), the collision-free set is
  {z_i − z_j ∉ ℤ[i] for i ≠ j}. Real-analytic functions on M_N correspond bijectively to
  real-analytic functions I on the collision-free subset of ℂ^N that are ℤ[i]-periodic in each
  z_i separately and invariant under the diagonal translations z ↦ z + (c,…,c), c ∈ ℂ: indeed
  every configuration on 𝕋^N can be translated into {Z = Z_0}, uniquely up to the stabiliser
  (1/N)ℤ[i]/ℤ[i], so M_N ≅ (𝕋^N ∖ Δ)/𝕋 (free action). For such I the canonical Hamiltonian
  vector field is tangent to the levels {Z = const} (since Σᵢ ∂I/∂xᵢ = Σᵢ ∂I/∂yᵢ = 0), the
  levels are symplectic submanifolds, and the reduced Poisson bracket of I and H equals the
  ambient one {I,H} = Σᵢ (∂_{xᵢ}I ∂_{yᵢ}H − ∂_{yᵢ}I ∂_{xᵢ}H). Hence "I is a first integral of the
  reduced flow" ⇔ {I,H} = 0 on the collision-free set. Partial derivatives are real Fréchet
  derivatives in the directions eᵢ and i·eᵢ.
* Functional independence: dI and dH linearly independent at some point (for analytic
  functions on the connected manifold M_N this is the same as independence on an open dense
  set). Translation-invariant functions have differentials vanishing on the diagonal
  directions, so independence in ℂ^N equals independence on M_N.
* The overall sign/normalisation of H (circulation, factor 2π) only rescales or reverses time
  and does not affect integrability.
* Proving `Claim` = no extra real-analytic integral for N = 3 (non-integrability).
  Proving `¬Claim` = such an integral exists (Liouville integrability on the 4-dimensional M_3).
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE090
noncomputable section

/-- The Gaussian integer lattice `ℤ + iℤ`. -/
def lattice : Set ℂ := {w : ℂ | ∃ m n : ℤ, w = (m : ℂ) + (n : ℂ) * Complex.I}

/-- Second directional derivative of `G` at `z` in the real direction `w`. -/
def d2 (G : ℂ → ℝ) (z w : ℂ) : ℝ :=
  deriv (fun s : ℝ => deriv (fun r : ℝ => G (z + (r : ℂ) * w)) s) 0

/-- Laplacian `∂²ₓG + ∂²_yG`. -/
def lapC (G : ℂ → ℝ) (z : ℂ) : ℝ := d2 G z 1 + d2 G z Complex.I

/-- `G` is the Green function of the square torus: `ΔG = δ₀ − 1`, up to an additive constant. -/
def IsTorusGreen (G : ℂ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ z : ℂ, G (z + 1) = G z ∧ G (z + Complex.I) = G z) ∧
  (∀ z : ℂ, z ∉ lattice → AnalyticAt ℝ G z) ∧
  (∀ z : ℂ, z ∉ lattice → lapC G z = -1) ∧
  (∃ C r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ ∀ z : ℂ, z ≠ 0 → ‖z‖ < r →
      |G z - Real.log ‖z‖ / (2 * Real.pi)| ≤ C)

/-- Collision-free configurations of `N` vortices (lifted to `ℂ^N`). -/
def collisionFree (N : ℕ) : Set (Fin N → ℂ) :=
  {z : Fin N → ℂ | ∀ i j : Fin N, i ≠ j → z i - z j ∉ lattice}

/-- The vortex Hamiltonian `H = −Σ_{i<j} G(zᵢ − zⱼ)` (identical unit circulations). -/
def ham (G : ℂ → ℝ) (N : ℕ) (z : Fin N → ℂ) : ℝ :=
  -∑ i : Fin N, ∑ j : Fin N, if i < j then G (z i - z j) else 0

/-- `∂F/∂xᵢ`. -/
def px {N : ℕ} (F : (Fin N → ℂ) → ℝ) (i : Fin N) (z : Fin N → ℂ) : ℝ :=
  fderiv ℝ F z (Pi.single i (1 : ℂ))

/-- `∂F/∂yᵢ`. -/
def py {N : ℕ} (F : (Fin N → ℂ) → ℝ) (i : Fin N) (z : Fin N → ℂ) : ℝ :=
  fderiv ℝ F z (Pi.single i Complex.I)

/-- Canonical Poisson bracket for `Σ dxᵢ ∧ dyᵢ`. -/
def poisson {N : ℕ} (F K : (Fin N → ℂ) → ℝ) (z : Fin N → ℂ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i : Fin N, (px F i z * py K i z - py F i z * px K i z)

/-- `I` is a real-analytic first integral of the reduced flow on `M_N`, functionally
independent of `H`. -/
def IsExtraIntegral (G : ℂ → ℝ) (N : ℕ) (I : (Fin N → ℂ) → ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ z ∈ collisionFree N, AnalyticAt ℝ I z) ∧
  (∀ z ∈ collisionFree N, ∀ i : Fin N,
      I (z + Pi.single i (1 : ℂ)) = I z ∧ I (z + Pi.single i Complex.I) = I z) ∧
  (∀ z ∈ collisionFree N, ∀ c : ℂ, I (z + fun _ => c) = I z) ∧
  (∀ z ∈ collisionFree N, poisson I (ham G N) z = 0) ∧
  (∃ z ∈ collisionFree N, ∀ a b : ℝ,
      a • fderiv ℝ I z + b • fderiv ℝ (ham G N) z = 0 → a = 0 ∧ b = 0)

/-- No extra analytic first integral for `N` identical vortices. -/
def NoExtraIntegral (G : ℂ → ℝ) (N : ℕ) : Prop := ¬ ∃ I : (Fin N → ℂ) → ℝ, IsExtraIntegral G N I

/-- Three identical vortices on the square torus are non-integrable. -/
def Claim : Prop :=
  (∃ G : ℂ → ℝ, IsTorusGreen G) ∧ ∀ G : ℂ → ℝ, IsTorusGreen G → NoExtraIntegral G 3

/-- Secondary target (not part of `Claim`): the same for four identical vortices. -/
def ClaimN4 : Prop :=
  (∃ G : ℂ → ℝ, IsTorusGreen G) ∧ ∀ G : ℂ → ℝ, IsTorusGreen G → NoExtraIntegral G 4

end
end OpenProblems.QEDE090
prov_reason: Non-integrability of three identical vortices on a periodic domain is the open case identified by the integrability classification (survey arXiv 2003.00716, Thm 7) and studied numerically by Borisov-Mamaev-Kilin; the rigorous statement is the natural open question they leave.

title: Cross-polytopes in 4D
credit: Klee & Wagon, Old and New Unsolved Problems in Plane Geometry and Number Theory (1991), Problem 11.5; V. V. Makeev (d = 3); R. Karasev, arXiv:0905.2671 (2009).
plain: Every smooth convex body in 4-space should have the eight corners of a regular cross-polytope lying on its boundary.
math: Prove that for every smooth convex body $K\subset\mathbb{R}^4$ there is a regular cross-polytope (a similar copy of $\mathrm{conv}\{\pm e_1,\dots,\pm e_4\}$) all of whose 8 vertices lie on $\partial K$.
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-E091: Cross-polytopes in 4D
Every smooth convex body in ℝ⁴ should have the eight vertices of some regular cross-polytope lying on
its boundary.
Informal statement: Prove that for every smooth convex body K ⊂ ℝ⁴ there is a regular cross-polytope
(a similar copy of conv{±e₁,…,±e₄}) all of whose 8 vertices lie on ∂K.
Formalization notes: ℝ⁴ is `Fin 4 → ℝ`; only its topology is used for compactness, convexity,
interior and frontier (the same as the Euclidean topology), and Euclidean geometry enters via the
explicit dot product `dot`. A smooth convex body is a compact convex set with nonempty interior that
has a global C^∞ defining function g (K = {g ≤ 0}, dg ≠ 0 on {g = 0}); this is equivalent to ∂K being
a C^∞ hypersurface. A regular cross-polytope (any similar copy, reflections allowed) is given by a
center c and four mutually orthogonal vectors u₁,…,u₄ of common length r > 0; its vertices are c ± uᵢ.
Proving `Claim` settles the case d = 4; proving `¬ Claim` means exhibiting a smooth convex body in ℝ⁴
with no inscribed regular cross-polytope.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE091

/-- ℝ⁴ as functions `Fin 4 → ℝ`. -/
abbrev R4 : Type := Fin 4 → ℝ

/-- Euclidean dot product. -/
def dot (u v : R4) : ℝ := ∑ k : Fin 4, u k * v k

/-- Compact convex body with nonempty interior and C^∞ boundary (via a defining function). -/
def IsSmoothConvexBody (K : Set R4) : Prop :=
  IsCompact K ∧ Convex ℝ K ∧ (interior K).Nonempty ∧
    ∃ g : R4 → ℝ, (∀ n : ℕ, ContDiff ℝ n g) ∧ K = {x | g x ≤ 0} ∧
      ∀ x : R4, g x = 0 → fderiv ℝ g x ≠ 0

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ K : Set R4, IsSmoothConvexBody K →
    ∃ (c : R4) (u : Fin 4 → R4) (r : ℝ), 0 < r ∧
      (∀ i : Fin 4, dot (u i) (u i) = r ^ 2) ∧
      (∀ i j : Fin 4, i ≠ j → dot (u i) (u j) = 0) ∧
      ∀ i : Fin 4, c + u i ∈ frontier K ∧ c - u i ∈ frontier K

end OpenProblems.QEDE091
prov_reason: Inscribing regular cross-polytopes in convex bodies is Klee-Wagon Problem 11.5; d = 4 is the first case left open after Makeev (d = 3) and Karasev (odd prime powers), and the notes say it is already posed implicitly.

title: Geodesic squares on convex surfaces
credit: Toeplitz 1911 (square peg problem); Schnirelmann 1944 (smooth case); constant-curvature surfaces: arXiv:2507.07945 (Naseri Sadr 2025)
premise_risks: arXiv:2507.07945 (2025 preprint, refereeing unclear): results for spheres and the hyperbolic plane; context only, Claim does not depend on it.
plain: On a smooth convex surface, measure distance by the length of the shortest path on the surface. Every smooth simple closed curve on the surface should contain four points that form a 'square' in this sense: four equal sides and two equal diagonals.
math: Let $S=\partial K$ for a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^3$ with smooth boundary and positive Gaussian curvature, and let $d$ be the intrinsic distance on $S$. Prove that every smooth simple closed curve $\gamma\subset S$ contains four distinct points $p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4$, in this cyclic order along $\gamma$, with $d(p_1,p_2)=d(p_2,p_3)=d(p_3,p_4)=d(p_4,p_1)>0$ and $d(p_1,p_3)=d(p_2,p_4)$.
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-E092: Geodesic squares on convex surfaces
On a smooth convex surface with positive curvature, measure distance by the length of the
shortest path on the surface. Does every smooth simple closed curve on the surface contain four
points, in cyclic order, forming an intrinsic "square": four equal positive sides and two equal
diagonals? This is the Toeplitz square peg problem moved to intrinsic geometry.
Informal statement: Let S = ∂K for a convex body K ⊂ R^3 with smooth boundary and positive
Gaussian curvature, and let d be the intrinsic distance on S. Prove that every smooth simple
closed curve γ ⊂ S contains four distinct points p1, p2, p3, p4, in this cyclic order along γ,
with d(p1,p2) = d(p2,p3) = d(p3,p4) = d(p4,p1) > 0 and d(p1,p3) = d(p2,p4).
Formalization notes: Space is `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)` (needed so that curve length uses the
Euclidean metric). The surface is S = {g = 0} for a C^∞ function g with K = {g <= 0} compact,
convex, with nonempty interior, ∇g ≠ 0 on S, and the Hessian of g positive definite on each
tangent plane ker dg(x), x ∈ S. With outward normal ∇g/|∇g| this says exactly that the second
fundamental form is positive definite, i.e. Gaussian curvature > 0; every smooth convex body
with positive curvature admits such a defining function. The intrinsic distance is the infimum,
in ℝ≥0∞, of the lengths (`eVariationOn` over [0,1]) of continuous paths in ℝ^3 with values in S
on [0,1] joining the points. A smooth simple closed curve is a C^∞ map γ : ℝ → ℝ^3 of period 1,
injective on [0,1), with nonvanishing derivative, lying in S. Cyclic order is encoded by
parameters t1 < t2 < t3 < t4 < t1 + 1 (so the four points are distinct). Proving Claim proves the
statement for all such surfaces and curves; ¬Claim requires a specific surface and curve with no
intrinsic inscribed square.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE092

/-- Euclidean 3-space. -/
abbrev E3 : Type := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)

/-- `S` is the boundary of a convex body with C^∞ boundary and positive Gaussian curvature,
given by a smooth defining function `g` (S = {g = 0}, body = {g <= 0}). -/
def IsSmoothPosCurvedConvexSurface (S : Set E3) : Prop :=
  ∃ g : E3 → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) g ∧
    S = {x | g x = 0} ∧
    IsCompact {x | g x ≤ 0} ∧ Convex ℝ {x | g x ≤ 0} ∧ (interior {x | g x ≤ 0}).Nonempty ∧
    (∀ x ∈ S, fderiv ℝ g x ≠ 0) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ S, ∀ v : E3, v ≠ 0 → fderiv ℝ g x v = 0 → 0 < fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ g) x v v)

/-- `γ` parametrizes a smooth simple closed curve lying in `S` (period 1). -/
def IsSmoothSimpleClosedCurveOn (S : Set E3) (γ : ℝ → E3) : Prop :=
  ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) γ ∧ (∀ t : ℝ, γ (t + 1) = γ t) ∧
    Set.InjOn γ (Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) 1) ∧ (∀ t : ℝ, deriv γ t ≠ 0) ∧ (∀ t : ℝ, γ t ∈ S)

/-- Intrinsic (path-length) distance on `S`, valued in ℝ≥0∞. -/
noncomputable def intrinsicDist (S : Set E3) (p q : E3) : ENNReal :=
  ⨅ (c : ℝ → E3) (_ : Continuous c) (_ : ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, c t ∈ S)
    (_ : c 0 = p) (_ : c 1 = q), eVariationOn c (Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Set E3, IsSmoothPosCurvedConvexSurface S →
    ∀ γ : ℝ → E3, IsSmoothSimpleClosedCurveOn S γ →
      ∃ t₁ t₂ t₃ t₄ : ℝ, t₁ < t₂ ∧ t₂ < t₃ ∧ t₃ < t₄ ∧ t₄ < t₁ + 1 ∧
        0 < intrinsicDist S (γ t₁) (γ t₂) ∧
        intrinsicDist S (γ t₁) (γ t₂) = intrinsicDist S (γ t₂) (γ t₃) ∧
        intrinsicDist S (γ t₂) (γ t₃) = intrinsicDist S (γ t₃) (γ t₄) ∧
        intrinsicDist S (γ t₃) (γ t₄) = intrinsicDist S (γ t₄) (γ t₁) ∧
        intrinsicDist S (γ t₁) (γ t₃) = intrinsicDist S (γ t₂) (γ t₄)

end OpenProblems.QEDE092
prov_reason: Moves the Toeplitz square peg problem (smooth case: Schnirelmann) from the plane to the intrinsic metric of a general positively curved convex surface; only constant-curvature surfaces have been treated.

title: Sofa stability
credit: Baek (2024), 'Optimality of Gerver's Sofa', arXiv:2411.19826.
premise_risks: arXiv:2411.19826 (Baek 2024; refereeing status unclear): the problem assumes Gerver's sofa is the maximizer. The formal Claim avoids this by quantifying over an unspecified stable sofa G, so it does not depend on Baek's result.
arXiv:2610.13955 (2026 preprint, cited in refs): context only; nothing in the statement depends on it.
plain: Baek (2024) proved that Gerver's sofa has the largest area among shapes that can be moved around a right-angled corner in a hallway of width 1. Show that any movable sofa whose area is nearly Gerver's must be nearly Gerver's sofa in shape (which in particular gives uniqueness).
math: A moving sofa is a compact connected $S\subset\mathbb R^2$ that can be moved by a continuous rigid motion from $(-\infty,0]\times[0,1]$ to $[0,1]\times(-\infty,0]$ inside $L=((-\infty,1]\times[0,1])\cup([0,1]\times(-\infty,1])$. Let $G$ be Gerver's sofa, of area $A_G\approx2.21953$. Prove that there are $C,\alpha>0$ such that every moving sofa $S$ with $|S|\ge A_G-\varepsilon$ satisfies $\min_{g}|gS\,\triangle\,G|\le C\varepsilon^{\alpha}$, the minimum over rigid motions $g$ of the plane.
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-E093: Sofa stability
Baek (2024) proved that Gerver's sofa has the largest area among shapes that can be moved around a right-angled corner
in a hallway of width 1. Show that any moving sofa whose area is within ε of the maximum is, after a rigid motion,
within C·ε^α of Gerver's sofa in symmetric-difference area (which in particular gives uniqueness of the maximizer).
Informal statement: A moving sofa is a compact connected S ⊂ ℝ² that can be moved by a continuous rigid motion from
(-∞,0]×[0,1] to [0,1]×(-∞,0] inside L = ((-∞,1]×[0,1]) ∪ ([0,1]×(-∞,1]). Let G be Gerver's sofa, of area A_G ≈ 2.21953.
Prove there are C, α > 0 such that every moving sofa S with |S| ≥ A_G − ε satisfies min_g |gS △ G| ≤ C ε^α, the
minimum over rigid motions g of the plane.
Formalization notes: Gerver's sofa (18 analytic boundary pieces with transcendental parameters) is not written down.
Instead Claim asserts that SOME moving sofa G is stable in this sense with respect to the supremum `maxArea` of sofa
areas. This is equivalent to the problem given Baek's theorem: if Claim holds for G, then applying it to a maximizing
sequence shows area G = maxArea and that every maximizer coincides with G up to a rigid motion and a null set, so
G is (a.e.) Gerver's sofa and the stability holds for Gerver's sofa; conversely Gerver's sofa witnesses Claim if the
stability statement is true. A rigid motion is p ↦ R_θ p + a (rotations and translations; reflections are not needed
since Gerver's sofa is mirror symmetric). The motion of the sofa is a pair of continuous functions θ, a on ℝ, used
on the time interval [0,1]. Area is Lebesgue measure on ℝ × ℝ, converted with `toReal` (finite for compact sets).
The minimum over g is replaced by "there exists g", which is equivalent up to the existential constant C.
Proving Claim = stability (and uniqueness); proving ¬Claim = for every sofa G and every C, α > 0 there are sofas of
area ≥ maxArea − ε that are farther than C ε^α from every rigid copy of G (e.g. non-uniqueness of the maximizer, or a
non-power-law stability rate).
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE093

/-- Rotation of the plane by angle `θ`. -/
noncomputable def rot (θ : ℝ) (p : ℝ × ℝ) : ℝ × ℝ :=
  (Real.cos θ * p.1 - Real.sin θ * p.2, Real.sin θ * p.1 + Real.cos θ * p.2)

/-- The rigid motion `p ↦ R_θ p + a`. -/
noncomputable def motion (θ : ℝ) (a : ℝ × ℝ) (p : ℝ × ℝ) : ℝ × ℝ := rot θ p + a

/-- The L-shaped hallway `((-∞,1] × [0,1]) ∪ ([0,1] × (-∞,1])`. -/
def hallway : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  {p | (p.1 ≤ 1 ∧ 0 ≤ p.2 ∧ p.2 ≤ 1) ∨ (0 ≤ p.1 ∧ p.1 ≤ 1 ∧ p.2 ≤ 1)}

/-- The starting arm `(-∞,0] × [0,1]`. -/
def startArm : Set (ℝ × ℝ) := {p | p.1 ≤ 0 ∧ 0 ≤ p.2 ∧ p.2 ≤ 1}

/-- The final arm `[0,1] × (-∞,0]`. -/
def endArm : Set (ℝ × ℝ) := {p | 0 ≤ p.1 ∧ p.1 ≤ 1 ∧ p.2 ≤ 0}

/-- `S` is a moving sofa: compact, connected, and movable through the hallway by a continuous rigid motion. -/
def IsMovingSofa (S : Set (ℝ × ℝ)) : Prop :=
  IsCompact S ∧ IsConnected S ∧
    ∃ θ : ℝ → ℝ, ∃ a : ℝ → ℝ × ℝ, Continuous θ ∧ Continuous a ∧
      (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, motion (θ t) (a t) '' S ⊆ hallway) ∧
      motion (θ 0) (a 0) '' S ⊆ startArm ∧
      motion (θ 1) (a 1) '' S ⊆ endArm

/-- Lebesgue area as a real number. -/
noncomputable def area (S : Set (ℝ × ℝ)) : ℝ := (MeasureTheory.volume S).toReal

/-- The supremum of the areas of moving sofas (equal to Gerver's constant by Baek's theorem). -/
noncomputable def maxArea : ℝ := sSup {r : ℝ | ∃ S : Set (ℝ × ℝ), IsMovingSofa S ∧ area S = r}

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∃ G : Set (ℝ × ℝ), IsMovingSofa G ∧
    ∃ C α : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ 0 < α ∧
      ∀ S : Set (ℝ × ℝ), IsMovingSofa S → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → maxArea - ε ≤ area S →
        ∃ θ : ℝ, ∃ a : ℝ × ℝ,
          area ((motion θ a '' S \ G) ∪ (G \ motion θ a '' S)) ≤ C * ε ^ α

end OpenProblems.QEDE093
prov_reason: A quantitative stability (and uniqueness) strengthening of Baek's optimality theorem for Gerver's sofa; no source poses the stability inequality.

title: Graceful labellings of forests
credit: Relaxation of the Ringel–Kotzig–Rosa Graceful Tree Conjecture; related: Van Bussel (EJC 2002, range-relaxed graceful labellings), Adamaszek–Allen–Grosu–Hladký arXiv:1608.01577, gracesize arXiv:2511.11331.
plain: A forest with m edges and c trees has m + c vertices. Label them with 0, 1, ..., m + c - 1, each label used once, so that the m edge differences |label(u) - label(v)| are all different. Show that every forest has such a labelling. The case 'a tree plus one isolated vertex' already says that every tree can be labelled gracefully if one spare label is allowed.
math: Prove that every forest $F$ with $m$ edges and $c\ge1$ components has a bijection $\ell:V(F)\to\{0,1,\dots,m+c-1\}$ such that the values $|\ell(u)-\ell(v)|$, $uv\in E(F)$, are pairwise distinct. (Key special case: $F=T\sqcup K_1$, i.e. every tree with $m$ edges has an injective labelling into $\{0,\dots,m+1\}$ with distinct edge differences.)
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-E094: Graceful labellings of forests
A forest with m edges and c trees has n = m + c vertices. Label them bijectively with
0, 1, …, n − 1 so that the m edge differences |ℓ(u) − ℓ(v)| are pairwise distinct. Show that
every forest has such a labelling. (The case tree + isolated vertex says every tree has an
injective labelling into {0, …, m+1} with distinct edge differences.)
Informal statement: Every forest F with m edges and c ≥ 1 components has a bijection
ℓ : V(F) → {0, 1, …, m + c − 1} such that the values |ℓ(u) − ℓ(v)|, uv ∈ E(F), are pairwise
distinct.
Formalization notes: A forest on n vertices is an acyclic `SimpleGraph (Fin n)`
(`SimpleGraph.IsAcyclic`); for a forest m + c = n, so the label set {0, …, m+c−1} is
{0, …, n−1} and a bijective labelling is an equivalence `ℓ : Fin n ≃ Fin n`. Differences are
computed in ℤ (no ℕ subtraction). "Pairwise distinct over edges" is: if two adjacent pairs
(u,v), (u',v') have equal differences then they are the same unordered edge. n = 0 (c = 0) is
included but trivial. Proving `Claim` proves the statement for all forests (it would follow
from the Graceful Tree Conjecture); `¬Claim` = an explicit forest with no such labelling.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE094

/-- A bijective labelling `ℓ : Fin n ≃ Fin n` of the vertices of `G` whose edge differences
are pairwise distinct. -/
def DistinctDiffLabelling {n : ℕ} (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) (ℓ : Fin n ≃ Fin n) : Prop :=
  ∀ u v u' v' : Fin n, G.Adj u v → G.Adj u' v' →
    |((ℓ u : ℕ) : ℤ) - ((ℓ v : ℕ) : ℤ)| = |((ℓ u' : ℕ) : ℤ) - ((ℓ v' : ℕ) : ℤ)| →
    (u = u' ∧ v = v') ∨ (u = v' ∧ v = u')

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), G.IsAcyclic →
    ∃ ℓ : Fin n ≃ Fin n, DistinctDiffLabelling G ℓ

end OpenProblems.QEDE094
M_fix_reason: M is correct and non-trivial (contains the open tree + K1 case); exhaustive search to 11 vertices found no counterexample.
prov_reason: A relaxation of the Graceful Tree Conjecture (one spare label per extra component); range-relaxed graceful labellings are studied but this forest formulation was not found in refs or search.

title: First-order convergence law for random Latin squares
results: Caution: route (i) as originally proposed has a flaw. The extension property 'every finite partial configuration extends in every consistent way w.h.p.' is false. A new x with x∘a1=b1 and x∘a2=b2 has expected count n·n^{-2}→0, because x∘a=b already determines x. The structure is functionally sparse (Lynch-type), not G(n,1/2)-type, so the route was rewritten.
premise_risks: arXiv:2606.18174 (Allsop-Morris, 2026 preprint): cited only as evidence that even the Poisson(1) idempotent law is unproved; the statement assumes nothing from it.
plain: Pick a Latin square of order n uniformly at random and read it as a multiplication table x∘y on n symbols. Does every first-order statement about this table have a limiting probability as n grows? A zero-one law fails: the number of x with x∘x=x should be asymptotically Poisson(1), so the probability that one exists should tend to 1−1/e rather than 0 or 1.
math: Let $L_n$ be uniform among Latin squares on $[n]$ and $\mathcal Q_n=([n],\circ)$ with $x\circ y=L_n(x,y)$. Prove or disprove: for every first-order sentence $\varphi$ in the language $\{\circ,=\}$, $\lim_{n\to\infty}\Pr[\mathcal Q_n\models\varphi]$ exists. (A 0-1 law should fail: by symbol-relabelling symmetry, $\mathbb E\#\{x:x\circ x=x\}=1$ exactly, and this count is conjecturally Poisson(1).) Expected route, as for Lynch's random unary functions: (i) w.h.p. the bounded-depth term closure of any bounded tuple is free except for coincidences counted by balanced configurations ($v$ elements, $v$ independent equations); (ii) a joint Poisson limit for the counts of all such balanced configurations, e.g. cycles of $x\mapsto x\circ x$. A disproof would need a definable sparse statistic with no limit law.
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-E095: First-order convergence law for random Latin squares
Pick a Latin square of order n uniformly at random and read it as a multiplication table x∘y on n
symbols. Does every first-order sentence about this quasigroup have a limiting probability as n → ∞?
(A zero-one law fails: the number of idempotents x∘x = x has mean exactly 1 and is conjecturally
Poisson(1).)
Informal statement: Let L_n be uniform among Latin squares on [n] and Q_n = ([n], ∘) with
x∘y = L_n(x,y). Prove or disprove: for every first-order sentence φ in the language {∘, =},
lim_{n→∞} Pr[Q_n ⊨ φ] exists.
Formalization notes: The language `qLang` has a single binary function symbol and no relation
symbols; equality is built into Mathlib's first-order logic (`FirstOrder.Language.Sentence`). A Latin
square of order n is a map L : Fin n → Fin n → Fin n whose rows and columns are bijections. The
structure `QG n L` is `Fin n` with `x ∘ y := L x y`. `satProb n φ` is the fraction of Latin squares of
order n satisfying φ (computed with `Set.ncard` on finite sets of functions; for n = 0 there is one
empty Latin square). `Claim` says every sentence has a real limit probability. Proving `¬ Claim`
means exhibiting a sentence whose satisfaction probability does not converge.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE095

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language

/-- Function symbols: one binary operation. -/
inductive QFunc : ℕ → Type
  | mul : QFunc 2

/-- The language `{∘}` of quasigroup multiplication tables (equality is built in). -/
def qLang : FirstOrder.Language where
  Functions := QFunc
  Relations := fun _ => Empty

/-- `L` is a Latin square: every row and every column is a bijection. -/
def IsLatin {n : ℕ} (L : Fin n → Fin n → Fin n) : Prop :=
  (∀ x : Fin n, Function.Bijective (L x)) ∧ (∀ y : Fin n, Function.Bijective (fun x => L x y))

/-- Carrier of the quasigroup given by the table `L` (a type synonym for `Fin n`). -/
def QG (n : ℕ) (_L : Fin n → Fin n → Fin n) : Type := Fin n

/-- Interpretation of the function symbols. -/
def QFunc.interp {n : ℕ} (L : Fin n → Fin n → Fin n) : {k : ℕ} → QFunc k → (Fin k → Fin n) → Fin n
  | _, QFunc.mul, xs => L (xs 0) (xs 1)

instance qgStructure (n : ℕ) (L : Fin n → Fin n → Fin n) : qLang.Structure (QG n L) where
  funMap := fun f xs => QFunc.interp L f xs
  RelMap := fun r _ => Empty.elim r

/-- Probability that a uniformly random Latin square of order `n` satisfies `φ`. -/
noncomputable def satProb (n : ℕ) (φ : qLang.Sentence) : ℝ :=
  (Set.ncard {L : Fin n → Fin n → Fin n | IsLatin L ∧ φ.Realize (QG n L)} : ℝ) /
    (Set.ncard {L : Fin n → Fin n → Fin n | IsLatin L} : ℝ)

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ φ : qLang.Sentence, ∃ ℓ : ℝ, Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => satProb n φ) Filter.atTop (nhds ℓ)

end OpenProblems.QEDE095
prov_reason: Reviewers found no prior work posing first-order convergence/zero-one laws for random Latin squares or quasigroups; the question is QED's own, modeled on Lynch-type laws.

title: Hat Ising universality
credit: Hat tiling: Smith, Myers, Kaplan, Goodman-Strauss (2023); numerics on hat-tiling Ising models as cited in the notes (arXiv:2402.11331, arXiv:2307.11054); background: Chelkak-Smirnov universality on isoradial graphs.
plain: Magnets on a hat tiling should behave at their critical point exactly like magnets on a square grid. Prove it.
math: Let T be any hat tiling (tiling of ℂ by isometric copies, reflections allowed, of the Smith–Myers–Kaplan–Goodman-Strauss hat; all such tilings form the hull) and G its tile-adjacency graph (tiles sharing a boundary segment), with the J=1 ferromagnetic Ising model. Prove: there is β_c ∈ (0,∞), the same for all T, such that, with constants c, C, δ > 0 depending only on T: (a) the plus-state magnetization M_T(β,x) = 0 for all tiles x and 0 ≤ β ≤ β_c, and c(β−β_c)^{1/8} ≤ M_T(β,x) ≤ C(β−β_c)^{1/8} uniformly in x for β_c < β < β_c+δ; (b) for β_c−δ < β < β_c, χ_T(β) = sup_x Σ_y ⟨σ_xσ_y⟩_β satisfies c(β_c−β)^{−7/4} ≤ χ_T(β) ≤ C(β_c−β)^{−7/4}; (c) for β_c−δ < β < β_c, the inverse correlation length 1/ξ_T(β) = liminf_{|x−y|→∞} (−log⟨σ_xσ_y⟩_β/|x−y|) satisfies c(β_c−β) ≤ 1/ξ_T(β) ≤ C(β_c−β).

import Mathlib
/-! QED-E096: Hat Ising universality
Magnets on a hat tiling should behave at their critical point exactly like magnets on a square grid. Prove it.
Informal statement (sharpened): Let `G` be the tile-adjacency graph of a hat tiling `T` (any tiling of the plane by
isometric copies, reflections allowed, of the Smith–Myers–Kaplan–Goodman-Strauss hat). Prove: there is
`β_c ∈ (0,∞)`, the same for all hat tilings `T`, such that, with constants depending only on `T`,
(a) `M_T(β, x) = 0` for all tiles `x` and `0 ≤ β ≤ β_c`, and `c(β−β_c)^{1/8} ≤ M_T(β, x) ≤ C(β−β_c)^{1/8}` uniformly in
`x` for `β_c < β < β_c + δ`; (b) for `β_c − δ < β < β_c`, `χ_T(β) = sup_x Σ_y ⟨σ_xσ_y⟩_β` satisfies
`c(β_c−β)^{−7/4} ≤ χ_T(β) ≤ C(β_c−β)^{−7/4}`; (c) for `β_c − δ < β < β_c`, the inverse correlation length
`1/ξ_T(β) = liminf_{|x−y|→∞} (−log⟨σ_xσ_y⟩_β / |x−y|)` satisfies `c(β_c−β) ≤ 1/ξ_T(β) ≤ C(β_c−β)`.
Formalization notes:
* Hat: the polykite with vertices (hex coordinates `(a,b) ↦ a + b/2 + i(√3/2)b`)
  (0,0),(−1,−1),(0,−2),(2,−2),(2,−1),(4,−2),(5,−1),(4,0),(3,0),(2,2),(0,3),(0,2),(−1,2) (Kaplan's coordinates; area
  `8√3`), written as the union of its 8 kites of the deltoidal trihexagonal grid (each kite = convex hull of hex
  centre, edge midpoint, vertex, edge midpoint), so no polygon-filling API is needed. The decomposition was checked
  numerically (8 kites, total area = polygon area).
* Hat tiling: a set `T` of tiles, each `g '' hat` for an isometry `g : ℂ ≃ᵢ ℂ`, covering `ℂ`, with pairwise
  disjoint interiors. "The hull" is taken to be the set of all hat tilings: by Smith et al. every hat tiling has the
  hierarchical metatile structure, so all hat tilings are locally isomorphic and form the hull (up to isometry).
  Adjacency: distinct tiles whose intersection contains a nondegenerate segment.
* Ising model, `J = 1`, on the (countable, locally finite) graph. Finite volume `Λ` (finite set of tiles), spins
  `±1`. Plus b.c.: weight `exp(β(Σ_{xy ⊂ Λ} σ_xσ_y + Σ_{x∈Λ} σ_x·#{y ∉ Λ adjacent to x}))`; free b.c.: no boundary
  term. Infinite-volume quantities: by GKS, `⟨σ_x⟩^+_Λ` decreases and free `⟨σ_xσ_y⟩_Λ` increases in `Λ`, so the
  thermodynamic limits equal the `inf` resp. `sup` over finite `Λ` (this is how they are defined). For `β < β_c`
  (`M^+ ≡ 0`) the Gibbs state is unique (Lebowitz–Martin-Löf), so free correlations are the correlations; there
  truncated = untruncated, so `χ` is the sum of `⟨σ_xσ_y⟩`. `χ` is valued in `ℝ≥0∞` (no summability junk).
* Distance between tiles: `inf_{a∈x} dist(a, y)`; tiles have bounded diameter so any reference point gives the
  same rates. The correlation-length bounds are written out: `1/ξ ≥ lo` iff for every `a < lo` all sufficiently
  distant pairs have `−log⟨σ_xσ_y⟩ ≥ a·|x−y|`; `1/ξ ≤ hi` iff for every `b > hi` there are arbitrarily distant pairs
  with `−log⟨σ_xσ_y⟩ ≤ b·|x−y|`.
* Judgement call: the problem's `1/ξ = −liminf (log⟨σ_xσ_y⟩/|x−y|)` takes the fastest-decaying pairs; we use the
  standard slowest-decay definition `1/ξ = liminf (−log⟨σ_xσ_y⟩/|x−y|)` (so `⟨σ_xσ_y⟩ ≤ e^{−(1/ξ−ε)|x−y|}` for
  all distant pairs), which is what "correlation length" means; also each asymptotic is placed on the side of
  `β_c` where the quantity is nontrivial, and constants depend on `T` but not on tiles.
* (a) is restricted to `0 ≤ β`: for `β < 0` (antiferromagnet) the plus-state magnetization is not 0
  (already `Λ = {x}` gives `tanh(β·deg x) < 0`, and `mag` is an infimum), which would make `Claim`
  false for a reason unrelated to criticality.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE096
noncomputable section
open scoped Classical
open Filter

/-- Hex-grid point `(a, b) ↦ a + b/2 + i·(√3/2)·b`. -/
def hexPt (a b : ℤ) : ℂ := ⟨(a : ℝ) + (b : ℝ) / 2, Real.sqrt 3 / 2 * (b : ℝ)⟩

/-- A kite with the given four grid vertices. -/
def kite (p q r s : ℤ × ℤ) : Set ℂ :=
  convexHull ℝ {hexPt p.1 p.2, hexPt q.1 q.2, hexPt r.1 r.2, hexPt s.1 s.2}

/-- The hat monotile, as a union of 8 kites. -/
def hat : Set ℂ :=
  kite (0, 0) (2, -1) (2, 0) (1, 1) ∪ kite (0, 0) (1, 1) (0, 2) (-1, 2) ∪
  kite (0, 0) (-1, -1) (0, -2) (1, -2) ∪ kite (0, 0) (1, -2) (2, -2) (2, -1) ∪
  kite (4, -2) (5, -1) (4, 0) (3, 0) ∪ kite (4, -2) (3, 0) (2, 0) (2, -1) ∪
  kite (2, 2) (0, 3) (0, 2) (1, 1) ∪ kite (2, 2) (1, 1) (2, 0) (3, 0)

/-- `T` is a tiling of the plane by hats (reflections allowed). -/
def IsHatTiling (T : Set (Set ℂ)) : Prop :=
  (∀ t ∈ T, ∃ g : ℂ ≃ᵢ ℂ, t = g '' hat) ∧ ⋃₀ T = Set.univ ∧
  ∀ s ∈ T, ∀ t ∈ T, s ≠ t → Disjoint (interior s) (interior t)

/-- Tile adjacency: distinct tiles sharing a boundary segment. -/
def Adj (T : Set (Set ℂ)) (x y : T) : Prop :=
  x ≠ y ∧ ∃ a b : ℂ, a ≠ b ∧ segment ℝ a b ⊆ (x : Set ℂ) ∩ (y : Set ℂ)

/-- Spin value of a Boolean. -/
def spin (b : Bool) : ℝ := if b then 1 else -1

/-- Spin at tile `x` for a configuration on `Λ` (plus outside `Λ`). -/
def sAt {T : Set (Set ℂ)} (Λ : Finset T) (σ : Λ → Bool) (x : T) : ℝ :=
  if h : x ∈ Λ then spin (σ ⟨x, h⟩) else 1

/-- `Σ_{x,y ∈ Λ, x ~ y} σ_x σ_y` over ordered pairs (each edge twice). -/
def bulk {T : Set (Set ℂ)} (Λ : Finset T) (σ : Λ → Bool) : ℝ :=
  ∑ x ∈ Λ, ∑ y ∈ Λ, if Adj T x y then sAt Λ σ x * sAt Λ σ y else 0

/-- Number of neighbours of `x` outside `Λ`. -/
def outDeg {T : Set (Set ℂ)} (Λ : Finset T) (x : T) : ℝ :=
  (({y : T | Adj T x y ∧ y ∉ Λ} : Set T).ncard : ℝ)

/-- Plus-boundary-condition Boltzmann weight. -/
def wPlus {T : Set (Set ℂ)} (β : ℝ) (Λ : Finset T) (σ : Λ → Bool) : ℝ :=
  Real.exp (β * (bulk Λ σ / 2 + ∑ x ∈ Λ, sAt Λ σ x * outDeg Λ x))

/-- Free-boundary-condition Boltzmann weight. -/
def wFree {T : Set (Set ℂ)} (β : ℝ) (Λ : Finset T) (σ : Λ → Bool) : ℝ :=
  Real.exp (β * (bulk Λ σ / 2))

/-- Finite-volume expectation. -/
def expect {T : Set (Set ℂ)} (Λ : Finset T) (w : (Λ → Bool) → ℝ) (f : (Λ → Bool) → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (∑ σ : Λ → Bool, f σ * w σ) / (∑ σ : Λ → Bool, w σ)

/-- Plus-state magnetization `⟨σ_x⟩^+_β` (thermodynamic limit = infimum over finite volumes). -/
def mag (T : Set (Set ℂ)) (β : ℝ) (x : T) : ℝ :=
  ⨅ Λ : {Λ : Finset T // x ∈ Λ}, expect Λ.1 (wPlus β Λ.1) (fun σ => sAt Λ.1 σ x)

/-- Two-point function `⟨σ_xσ_y⟩_β` (free state; thermodynamic limit = supremum over finite volumes). -/
def corr (T : Set (Set ℂ)) (β : ℝ) (x y : T) : ℝ :=
  ⨆ Λ : {Λ : Finset T // x ∈ Λ ∧ y ∈ Λ},
    expect Λ.1 (wFree β Λ.1) (fun σ => sAt Λ.1 σ x * sAt Λ.1 σ y)

/-- Susceptibility `sup_x Σ_y ⟨σ_xσ_y⟩_β`. -/
def susc (T : Set (Set ℂ)) (β : ℝ) : ENNReal :=
  ⨆ x : T, ∑' y : T, ENNReal.ofReal (corr T β x y)

/-- Distance between tiles. -/
def tileDist (s t : Set ℂ) : ℝ := ⨅ a : s, Metric.infDist (a : ℂ) t

/-- `lo ≤ 1/ξ_T(β) ≤ hi`, with `1/ξ = liminf_{|x−y|→∞} (−log⟨σ_xσ_y⟩ / |x−y|)`. -/
def InvCorrLengthBetween (T : Set (Set ℂ)) (β lo hi : ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ a : ℝ, a < lo → ∃ R : ℝ, ∀ x y : T, R ≤ tileDist (x : Set ℂ) (y : Set ℂ) →
      a * tileDist (x : Set ℂ) (y : Set ℂ) ≤ -Real.log (corr T β x y)) ∧
  (∀ b : ℝ, hi < b → ∀ R : ℝ, ∃ x y : T, R ≤ tileDist (x : Set ℂ) (y : Set ℂ) ∧
      -Real.log (corr T β x y) ≤ b * tileDist (x : Set ℂ) (y : Set ℂ))

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∃ βc : ℝ, 0 < βc ∧ ∀ T : Set (Set ℂ), IsHatTiling T →
    (∀ β : ℝ, 0 ≤ β → β ≤ βc → ∀ x : T, mag T β x = 0) ∧
    ∃ δ c C : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ 0 < c ∧ 0 < C ∧
      (∀ β : ℝ, βc < β → β < βc + δ → ∀ x : T,
        c * (β - βc) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 8) ≤ mag T β x ∧ mag T β x ≤ C * (β - βc) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / 8)) ∧
      (∀ β : ℝ, βc - δ < β → β < βc →
        ENNReal.ofReal (c * (βc - β) ^ (-(7 : ℝ) / 4)) ≤ susc T β ∧
        susc T β ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * (βc - β) ^ (-(7 : ℝ) / 4))) ∧
      (∀ β : ℝ, βc - δ < β → β < βc →
        InvCorrLengthBetween T β (c * (βc - β)) (C * (βc - β)))

end
end OpenProblems.QEDE096
M_fix_reason: M leaves ambiguous which side of β_c each exponent refers to (χ and ξ are usually stated for β < β_c, and the susceptibility on an aperiodic graph needs a sup/average over base points), and whether the asymptotics must be uniform in the base tile; the fix pins these down.
prov_reason: Instance of the broad open problem of Ising universality on aperiodic/non-isoradial planar graphs, specialized to the hat tiling; the hat case has only been studied by Monte Carlo.

title: Irrationality of the quartic oscillator ground state
plain: The lowest energy of the quartic oscillator, -d^2/dx^2 + x^4 on the line, is about 1.0603620905. Show that it is irrational.
math: Let $E_0=\min\sigma\big(-\tfrac{d^2}{dx^2}+x^4\big)$, the operator taken self-adjoint on $L^2(\mathbb R)$ ($E_0=1.06036209048418\ldots$). Prove that $E_0\notin\mathbb Q$.
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-E097: Irrationality of the quartic oscillator ground state
The lowest energy of the quartic oscillator −d²/dx² + x⁴ on the line is about 1.0603620905.
Show that it is irrational.
Informal statement: Let E₀ = min σ(−d²/dx² + x⁴), the operator taken self-adjoint on L²(ℝ)
(E₀ = 1.06036209048418…). Prove that E₀ ∉ ℚ.
Formalization notes:
* E₀ is defined variationally: E₀ = inf over nonzero real φ ∈ C_c^1(ℝ) of the Rayleigh quotient
  (∫ φ'² + x⁴ φ²) / ∫ φ². By the min-max principle, E₀ = inf σ(H) for the Friedrichs
  (= unique, since x⁴ ≥ 0 and C_c^∞ is a core) self-adjoint realization, because C_c^1 lies
  in the form domain and contains C_c^∞, which is a form core. Restricting to real φ loses
  nothing: for φ = u + iv the quotient is a weighted average of those of u and v.
* C^1 (`ContDiff ℝ 1`) is used deliberately instead of `ContDiff ℝ ⊤`, which in current Mathlib
  may mean analytic and would make the set empty. For continuous compactly supported
  integrands the Bochner integrals are the genuine integrals, and φ ≠ 0 with φ continuous
  makes the denominator positive. The set is nonempty and bounded below by 0, so `sInf` is
  the true infimum.
* Proving `Claim`: E₀ is irrational. Proving `¬Claim`: E₀ is rational.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE097

/-- The Rayleigh quotient of `−d²/dx² + x⁴` at `φ`. -/
noncomputable def rayleighQuotient (φ : ℝ → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (∫ x : ℝ, (deriv φ x) ^ 2 + x ^ 4 * (φ x) ^ 2) / (∫ x : ℝ, (φ x) ^ 2)

/-- The ground state energy `E₀` of the quartic oscillator, defined variationally. -/
noncomputable def groundStateEnergy : ℝ :=
  sInf {E : ℝ | ∃ φ : ℝ → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 φ ∧ HasCompactSupport φ ∧ φ ≠ 0 ∧
    E = rayleighQuotient φ}

def Claim : Prop := Irrational groundStateEnergy

end OpenProblems.QEDE097
prov_reason: Reviewer found no literature posing the arithmetic nature of the quartic oscillator ground state energy.

title: Break the 5/8 barrier for primes with triply well-factorable weights
credit: A. Pascadi, arXiv:2505.00653 (2025), Thm 1.3 and remarks on the 5/8 limit; J. D. Lichtman, arXiv:2309.08522 (2023); triply well-factorable weights from Maynard's equidistribution papers.
premise_risks: arXiv:2505.00653 (Pascadi, 2025 preprint, refereeing status unverified): the known baseline θ* ≥ 5/8 unconditionally and the exact definition of triply well-factorable weights (Def 1.1) are taken from it.
arXiv:2602.20917 and arXiv:2608.13299 (2026 preprints): used only to check that no one has passed 5/8; the statement assumes nothing from them.
plain: The primes are known to be evenly spread over residue classes, on average over moduli up to x^{5/8}, if the average is weighted by triply well-factorable weights. Push the exponent past 5/8, or show the dispersion method cannot.
math: Say (lambda_q)_{q<=Q} is triply well-factorable of level Q if for all Q1Q2Q3=Q there are 1-bounded alpha,beta,gamma supported on q_i<=Q_i with lambda=alpha*beta*gamma (Dirichlet convolution). Let theta* = sup of theta such that for all eps,A>0, fixed a!=0, and every such lambda of level Q=x^{theta-eps}: sum_{q<=Q,(q,a)=1} lambda_q(pi(x;q,a)-pi(x)/phi(q)) <<_{eps,A,a} x(log x)^{-A}. Known theta*>=5/8 (Pascadi). Prove theta*>5/8.
lean:
import Mathlib
/-! QED-E098: Break the 5/8 barrier for primes with triply well-factorable weights
Primes are equidistributed in residue classes on average over moduli q up to x^{5/8-ε} when the
average is weighted by triply well-factorable weights (Pascadi 2025). The problem is to push the
exponent beyond 5/8.
Informal statement: Say (λ_q)_{q ≤ Q} is triply well-factorable of level Q if for all Q₁Q₂Q₃ = Q
there are 1-bounded α, β, γ supported on q_i ≤ Q_i with λ = α * β * γ (Dirichlet convolution).
Let θ* be the sup of θ such that for all ε, A > 0, fixed a ≠ 0, and every such λ of level
Q = x^{θ-ε}: ∑_{q ≤ Q, (q,a)=1} λ_q (π(x;q,a) − π(x)/φ(q)) ≪_{ε,A,a} x (log x)^{-A}.
Known θ* ≥ 5/8 (Pascadi). Prove θ* > 5/8.
Formalization notes: Weights are complex. "Triply well-factorable of level Q" requires, for every
real Q₁, Q₂, Q₃ ≥ 1 with Q₁Q₂Q₃ = Q, sequences α, β, γ with |·| ≤ 1 supported on [1, Q_i] whose
triple Dirichlet convolution is λ (so λ is automatically supported on [1, Q]). π(x;q,a) counts primes
p ≤ x with p ≡ a (mod q); π(x) counts primes p ≤ x; φ = Nat.totient. The implied constant C and the
threshold x₀ may depend on θ, ε, A, a but must be uniform in λ. Since the property for θ implies it
for every smaller θ (absorb θ − θ' into ε), "θ* > 5/8" is equivalent to the existence of some
θ > 5/8 with the property, which is what `Claim` says. Proving `Claim` breaks the 5/8 barrier;
proving `¬ Claim` would show that 5/8 is the true limit for this class of weights (a barrier
theorem). Known: the property holds for θ = 5/8 (Pascadi, arXiv:2505.00653, Thm 1.3).
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE098

/-- `α` is 1-bounded and supported on integers in `[1, Q]`. -/
def BoundedSupported (Q : ℝ) (α : ℕ → ℂ) : Prop :=
  (∀ n : ℕ, ‖α n‖ ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, α n ≠ 0 → 1 ≤ n ∧ (n : ℝ) ≤ Q)

/-- Triple Dirichlet convolution `(α * β * γ)(q) = ∑_{abc = q} α(a) β(b) γ(c)`. -/
noncomputable def conv3 (α β γ : ℕ → ℂ) (q : ℕ) : ℂ :=
  ∑ a ∈ q.divisors, ∑ b ∈ (q / a).divisors, α a * β b * γ (q / a / b)

/-- Triply well-factorable weights of level `Q`. -/
def TriplyWellFactorable (Q : ℝ) (w : ℕ → ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∀ Q₁ Q₂ Q₃ : ℝ, 1 ≤ Q₁ → 1 ≤ Q₂ → 1 ≤ Q₃ → Q₁ * Q₂ * Q₃ = Q →
    ∃ α β γ : ℕ → ℂ, BoundedSupported Q₁ α ∧ BoundedSupported Q₂ β ∧ BoundedSupported Q₃ γ ∧
      ∀ q : ℕ, w q = conv3 α β γ q

open Classical in
/-- `π(x)`: number of primes `p ≤ x`. -/
noncomputable def primeCount (x : ℝ) : ℕ :=
  ((Finset.range (⌊x⌋₊ + 1)).filter (fun p => Nat.Prime p)).card

open Classical in
/-- `π(x; q, a)`: number of primes `p ≤ x` with `p ≡ a (mod q)`. -/
noncomputable def primeCountAP (x : ℝ) (q : ℕ) (a : ℤ) : ℕ :=
  ((Finset.range (⌊x⌋₊ + 1)).filter
    (fun p => Nat.Prime p ∧ (p : ℤ) % (q : ℤ) = a % (q : ℤ))).card

/-- `π(x;q,a) − π(x)/φ(q)`. -/
noncomputable def discrepancy (x : ℝ) (q : ℕ) (a : ℤ) : ℝ :=
  (primeCountAP x q a : ℝ) - (primeCount x : ℝ) / (Nat.totient q : ℝ)

open Classical in
/-- The weighted sum `∑_{q ≤ Q, (q,a)=1} w_q (π(x;q,a) − π(x)/φ(q))`. -/
noncomputable def weightedSum (x Q : ℝ) (a : ℤ) (w : ℕ → ℂ) : ℂ :=
  ∑ q ∈ ((Finset.Icc 1 ⌊Q⌋₊ : Finset ℕ).filter (fun q : ℕ => Int.gcd (q : ℤ) a = 1)),
    w q * ((discrepancy x q a : ℝ) : ℂ)

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∃ θ : ℝ, 5 / 8 < θ ∧
    ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ A : ℝ, 0 < A → ∀ a : ℤ, a ≠ 0 →
      ∃ C x₀ : ℝ, ∀ x : ℝ, x₀ ≤ x → ∀ w : ℕ → ℂ,
        TriplyWellFactorable (x ^ (θ - ε)) w →
          ‖weightedSum x (x ^ (θ - ε)) a w‖ ≤ C * x * (Real.log x) ^ (-A)

end OpenProblems.QEDE098
prov_reason: Passing the 5/8 exponent for triply well-factorable weights is the explicit frontier identified by Pascadi (who calls 5/8 the apparent limit of current technology), following Lichtman's work; QED only packages it.

title: Close the gap in the density of integers that are sums of two rational cubes
credit: Alpöge, Bhargava, Shnidman, Integers expressible as the sum of two rational cubes, arXiv:2210.10730 (2022); Koymans-Smith arXiv:2606.06024 (2026) for the complement side.

plain: BSD plus the minimalist rank heuristic predict that exactly half of all integers are sums of two rational cubes. Proven: at least 2/21 are (Alpöge–Bhargava–Shnidman), and at least 31.95% are not (Koymans–Smith). Improve either bound.
math: Let $\mathcal S=\{n\in\mathbb Z: n=x^3+y^3,\ x,y\in\mathbb Q\}$ and $d_\pm$ the lower densities of $\mathcal S$ and of its complement (ordered by $|n|$). Known: $\underline d(\mathcal S)\ge 2/21$, $\underline d(\mathcal S^c)\ge 0.3195$. Conjecture: both densities equal $1/2$. Improve either constant.

BSD plus rank heuristics predict that half of all integers are sums of two rational cubes. Proven: at least 2/21 are (Alpöge-Bhargava-Shnidman) and at least 31.95% are not (Koymans-Smith). This file asks to improve the 2/21.
Informal statement: Let $\mathcal S=\{n\in\mathbb Z: n=x^3+y^3,\ x,y\in\mathbb Q\}$ and $d_\pm$ the lower densities of $\mathcal S$ and of its complement (ordered by $|n|$). namespace OpenProblems.QEDE099

/-- `n` is a sum of two rational cubes. -/
def IsSumTwoRatCubes (n : ℕ) : Prop := ∃ x y : ℚ, (n : ℚ) = x ^ 3 + y ^ 3

/-- The number of `n ∈ [1, N]` that are sums of two rational cubes. -/
noncomputable def countS (N : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Nat.card {n : ℕ // 1 ≤ n ∧ n ≤ N ∧ IsSumTwoRatCubes n}

/-- The lower density of positive integers that are sums of two rational cubes exceeds `2/21`. -/
def Claim : Prop :=
  ∃ c : ℝ, (2 : ℝ) / 21 < c ∧ ∃ N₀ : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, N₀ ≤ N → c * (N : ℝ) ≤ (countS N : ℝ)

end OpenProblems.QEDE099
prov_reason: Improving the Alpöge-Bhargava-Shnidman proportions toward the conjectured 1/2 is the natural open problem stated in that line of work.

title: Improve H_1 <= 12 under EH alone
credit: D.H.J. Polymath 2014, arXiv:1407.4897; J. Maynard 2015, arXiv:1311.4600
plain: Assuming Elliott–Halberstam, Maynard's sieve gives infinitely many pairs of primes at distance at most 12. The generalized conjecture GEH gives 6. Lower 12 using EH alone.
math: Let $H_1=\liminf_{n}(p_{n+1}-p_n)$. Assuming EH (level $\theta=1-\varepsilon$ for all $\varepsilon>0$, for the von Mangoldt function only, not GEH), prove $H_1\le 10$, or prove that no Selberg/Maynard-type sieve weight using EH alone can give $H_1<12$.

/-! QED-E100: Improve H_1 ≤ 12 under EH alone
Assuming the Elliott–Halberstam conjecture, Maynard's sieve gives infinitely many pairs of primes at
distance at most 12 (GEH gives 6). Lower 12 using EH alone.
Informal statement: Let H₁ = liminf_n (p_{n+1} − p_n). Assuming EH (level θ = 1 − ε for every ε > 0,
for the von Mangoldt function only, not GEH), prove H₁ ≤ 10. (The alternative "prove that no
Selberg/Maynard-type sieve weight using EH alone can give H₁ < 12" concerns a class of methods and is
not formalized.)

max is encoded by quantifying over every choice function a(q) of residues coprime to q (equivalent).
H₁ ≤ 10 ⇔ infinitely many primes p with another prime in (p, p+10].

proving H₁ ≤ 10 also proves Claim). Proving `¬Claim` would require proving EH and H₁ > 10, i.e. is
not a realistic route. Caution for reviewers: if `EH` were mis-stated so as to be false, Claim would
be vacuous; the statement here is the standard one (θ < 1/2 is Bombieri–Vinogradov).
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE100

/-- ψ(x; q, a). -/
noncomputable def psiAP (x : ℝ) (q a : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ n ∈ (Finset.Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊).filter (fun n => n % q = a % q), ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n

/-- ψ(x). -/
noncomputable def psi (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 ⌊x⌋₊, ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt n

/-- The Elliott–Halberstam conjecture. -/
def EH : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ A : ℝ, 0 < A → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x : ℝ, 2 ≤ x →
    ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ q, Nat.Coprime (a q) q) →
      ∑ q ∈ Finset.Icc 1 ⌊x ^ (1 - ε)⌋₊,
          |psiAP x q (a q) - psi x / (Nat.totient q : ℝ)| ≤ C * x / Real.log x ^ A

def Claim : Prop :=
  EH → ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ p q : ℕ, N < p ∧ p.Prime ∧ q.Prime ∧ p < q ∧ q ≤ p + 10

end OpenProblems.QEDE100
prov_reason: Polymath8b records H_1 <= 12 under EH (and 6 under GEH) and discusses the limits of the sieve; lowering 12 under EH alone is the open question left there.

title: Interval-sieve extremal bounds behind the Banks–Ford–Tao gap prediction
credit: Banks, Ford, Tao, Large prime gaps and probabilistic models, Invent. Math. 2023 (arXiv:1908.08613)
plain: Banks, Ford and Tao showed that a random sieve model of the primes predicts the largest prime gap below x is about g(ξ log²x), where g is controlled by an extremal sieve quantity W_y. W_y is the fewest survivors in [0,y] after one residue class is removed for each prime up to √(y/log y). Narrow the bounds on W_y.
math: Let W_y = min over residue choices (a_p) of #{n ∈ [0,y] ∩ ℤ : n ≢ a_p (mod p) for all primes p <= (y/log y)^{1/2}}. Known (Banks-Ford-Tao): (4+o(1)) y log log y/log^2 y <= W_y <= y/log y + O(y log log y/log^2 y). Prove or disprove: there is an absolute c > 0 with W_y >= c·y/log y for all sufficiently large y.

prime gaps. Is W_y of order y / log y?
Informal statement: Let W_y = min over residue choices (a_p) of #{n ∈ [0,y] ∩ ℤ : n ≢ a_p (mod p) for all primes p <= (y/log y)^{1/2}}. Formalization notes: Integers in [0, y] are the naturals m <= ⌊y⌋. A residue choice is any
function a : ℕ → ℕ, with a p read modulo p (this covers all choices of one class per prime).
Survivors are m with m ≢ a p (mod p) for every prime p with p <= √(y / log y). The lower bound

survivors is at least c y / log y (so the minimum need not be defined). Proving Claim gives the

/-- Survivors in [0, y] of the sieve removing the class `a p mod p` for each prime

title: Largest prime factor of Markov numbers
credit: Extends Corvaja–Zannier, 'On the greatest prime factor of Markov pairs', Rend. Sem. Mat. Univ. Padova 116 (2006).
plain: Markov numbers are the numbers appearing in positive integer solutions of x^2+y^2+z^2=3xyz. Show that the largest prime factor of a Markov number tends to infinity. Equivalently, for any finite set of primes, only finitely many Markov numbers are built from those primes alone.
math: Let $\mathcal M=\{m\ge1:\exists\,x,y\in\mathbb Z_{>0},\ x^2+y^2+m^2=3xym\}$ and let $P(m)$ denote the largest prime factor of $m$ (with $P(1)=1$). Prove that $P(m)\to\infty$ as $m\to\infty$ in $\mathcal M$; equivalently, for every finite set $S$ of primes, only finitely many $m\in\mathcal M$ are $S$-units.

import Mathlib
/-! QED-E102: Largest prime factor of Markov numbers
Markov numbers are the numbers appearing in positive integer solutions of x² + y² + z² = 3xyz.
Show that the largest prime factor of a Markov number tends to infinity; equivalently, for any
finite set of primes only finitely many Markov numbers are built from those primes alone.
Informal statement: Let 𝓜 = {m ≥ 1 : ∃ x, y ∈ ℤ_{>0}, x² + y² + m² = 3xym} and P(m) the largest
prime factor of m (P(1) = 1). Prove that P(m) → ∞ as m → ∞ in 𝓜; equivalently, for every
finite set S of primes, only finitely many m ∈ 𝓜 are S-units.
Formalization notes: The Claim is the S-unit form: for every finite set S ⊆ ℕ, the set of
Markov numbers all of whose prime divisors lie in S is finite. (Non-primes in S are harmless.)
This is equivalent to P(m) → ∞ along 𝓜. Everything is in ℕ with no subtraction. Proving
`Claim` = the conjecture; `¬Claim` = a finite set of primes supporting infinitely many Markov
numbers.
-/
namespace OpenProblems.QEDE102

/-- `m` is a Markov number. -/
def IsMarkov (m : ℕ) : Prop :=
  1 ≤ m ∧ ∃ x y : ℕ, 0 < x ∧ 0 < y ∧ x ^ 2 + y ^ 2 + m ^ 2 = 3 * x * y * m

def Claim : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Finset ℕ,
    Set.Finite {m : ℕ | IsMarkov m ∧ ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → p ∣ m → p ∈ S}

end OpenProblems.QEDE102
prov_reason: Single-number strengthening of Corvaja–Zannier's theorem that the greatest prime factor of xy over Markov pairs tends to infinity; not found posed explicitly (notes uncertain, one search found nothing).

title: Lower the exponent 0.7785 for A4-quartic fields
credit: Bhargava, Shankar, Taniguchi, Thorne, Tsimerman, Zhao, 'Bounds on 2-torsion in class groups of number fields and integral points on elliptic curves', JAMS 2020 (arXiv:1701.02458, Thm 1.4); Loughran-Paterson arXiv:2510.05248
premise_risks: arXiv:2510.05248 (Loughran-Paterson, 2025 preprint): lower bound X^{1/2} log X and the statement that 0.7784... is the current record; the Claim itself depends only on the refereed BSTTTZ exponent.
arXiv:2602.23619 (Alberts-Bucur, 2026 preprint): cited only for the status 'no 2026 improvement'.
plain: Malle predicts about X^{1/2} log X quartic fields with Galois group A4 and discriminant up to X. Loughran–Paterson (2025) proved the matching lower bound. The best upper bound is still about X^{0.7785}. Lower the exponent.
math: Let N_{A4}(X) count quartic L/Q with Gal(L~/Q)=A4 and |Delta_L|<=X. Known: X^{1/2} log X << N_{A4}(X) << X^{0.7784...+eps} (Loughran-Paterson arXiv:2510.05248 Thm 1.1; BSTTTZ JAMS 2020 Thm 1.4). Prove N_{A4}(X) << X^{beta} for some beta<0.7784 (ideally beta=1/2+eps).
